title.en: Volume 172 Biographies 122: Ling Huchu, Niu Sengru, Xiaomian, Li Shi
title.raw: 卷一百七十二 列傳第一百二十二: 令狐楚 牛僧孺 蕭俛 李石 Volume 172 Biographies 122: Ling Huchu, Niu Sengru, Xiaomian, Li Shi

sentences.zh: 李宗閔李宗閔，字損之，宗室鄭王元懿之後。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin, styled Sunzhi, was a descendant of Prince Yuanyi of Zheng among the imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin, whose courtesy name was Sunzhi, was a descendant of Prince Yuanyi of Zheng from the imperial family.

sentences.zh: 祖自仙，楚州別駕。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zixian served as Vice Prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zixian had been vice prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父，宗正卿，出為華州刺史、鎮國軍潼關防禦等使。

translations.literal: His father served as Director of the Imperial Clan Court, then went out as Governor of Huazhou and Commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and Tongguan Defense, among other duties.
translations.idiomatic: His father served as director of the Imperial Clan Court before being sent out as governor of Huazhou and commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and Tongguan defense, among other posts.

sentences.zh: 兄夷簡，元和中宰相。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yijian was a chief minister during the Yuanhe era.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yijian had served as chief minister during the Yuanhe reign.

sentences.zh: 宗閔，進士擢第，，復登制舉賢良方正科。

translations.literal: Zongmin passed the jinshi examination and also passed the special examination for outstanding and upright men of worth.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin passed the jinshi examination and later also passed the special civil-service examination for outstanding and upright men of worth.

sentences.zh: 初，宗閔與牛僧孺同年登進士第，又與僧孺同年登制科。

translations.literal: At first, Zongmin and Niu Sengru passed the jinshi in the same year, and they also passed the special examination in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Zongmin and Niu Sengru had passed the jinshi examination in the same year, and they also passed the special examination in the same year.

sentences.zh: 應制之歲，李吉甫為宰相當國，宗閔、僧孺對策，指切時政之失，言甚鯁直，無所回避。

translations.literal: In the year they took the special examination, Li Jifu was chief minister directing the state. Zongmin and Sengru submitted their policy responses, directly criticizing the faults of current governance. Their words were very blunt and unyielding, and they did not evade anything.
translations.idiomatic: In the year they took the special examination, Li Jifu was chief minister and directed the government. Zongmin and Sengru submitted their policy essays, directly criticizing the failings of current policy. Their language was blunt and unyielding, and they held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 考策官楊於陵、韋貫之、李益等又第其策為中等，又為不中第者註解牛、李策語，同為唱誹。

translations.literal: The examiners Yang Yuling, Wei Guanzhi, Li Yi, and others also ranked their essays in the middle tier. They also annotated the policy essays of Niu and Li for those who had not passed, together indulging in mutual ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: The examiners Yang Yuling, Wei Guanzhi, Li Yi, and others also ranked their essays in the middle tier. They further annotated Niu and Li's policy essays for those who had failed the examination, joining together in mutual mockery.

sentences.zh: 又言翰林學士王涯甥皇甫湜中選，考核之際，不先上言。

translations.literal: They also said that Huangfu Shi, nephew of Hanlin Academician Wang Ya, had been selected, and that during the evaluation they had not first reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: They also charged that Huangfu Shi, nephew of Hanlin academician Wang Ya, had been selected, and that during the evaluation the examiners had not first reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 裴垍時為學士，居中覆視，無所異同。

translations.literal: Pei Ji was then a Hanlin academician and reviewed the papers from within the palace. He found nothing amiss.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji was then a Hanlin academician and reviewed the papers from within the palace, finding nothing out of order.

sentences.zh: 吉甫泣訴於上前，憲宗不獲已，罷王涯、裴垍學士。

translations.literal: Jifu wept and complained before the emperor. Emperor Xianzong had no choice but to remove Wang Ya and Pei Ji as Hanlin academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu wept and complained before the emperor. Emperor Xianzong, unable to do otherwise, removed Wang Ya and Pei Ji from their Hanlin posts.

sentences.zh: 垍守戶部侍郎，涯守都官員外郎，吏部尚書楊於陵出為嶺南節度使，吏部員外郎韋貫之出為果州刺史。

translations.literal: Ji remained as Vice Minister of Revenue; Ya remained as Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; Minister of Personnel Yang Yuling was sent out as military governor of Lingnan; and Vice Director of Personnel Wei Guanzhi was sent out as prefect of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Ji retained his post as vice minister of revenue; Ya retained his post as vice director in the Ministry of Justice; Minister of Personnel Yang Yuling was sent out as military governor of Lingnan; and Vice Director of Personnel Wei Guanzhi was sent out as prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 王涯再貶虢州司馬，貫之再貶巴州刺史；

translations.literal: Wang Ya was demoted again to Assistant Administrator of Guo Prefecture; Guanzhi was demoted again to prefect of Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya was demoted again to assistant administrator of Guo Prefecture, and Guanzhi was demoted again to prefect of Ba.

sentences.zh: 僧孺、宗閔亦久之不調，隨牒諸侯府。

translations.literal: Sengru and Zongmin also went long without appointment and attached themselves to various feudatory staff offices.
translations.idiomatic: Sengru and Zongmin also went long without regular appointment and took staff positions in various regional administrations.

sentences.zh: 七年，吉甫卒，方入朝為監察御史，累遷禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when Jifu died, Zongmin finally entered court as a supervisory censor and was promoted in succession to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after Jifu died, Zongmin finally entered court as a supervisory censor and was promoted in succession to vice director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: ，宰相裴度出征吳元濟，奏宗閔為彰義軍觀察判官。

translations.literal: When chief minister Pei Du marched against Wu Yuanji, he memorialized that Zongmin serve as administrative aide to the Zhangyi observation envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When chief minister Pei Du marched against Wu Yuanji, he recommended that Zongmin serve as administrative aide to the Zhangyi observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊平，遷駕部郎中，又以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites for the Department of Transport and, retaining his original rank, was also put in charge of drafting imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were pacified, he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites for the Department of Transport and, while retaining that rank, was also put in charge of drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Zongmin was appointed Vice Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Zongmin was appointed vice director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時自宗正卿出刺華州，父子同時承恩制，人士榮之。

translations.literal: At that time his father had gone out from Director of the Imperial Clan Court to serve as prefect of Huazhou, and father and son at the same time received edicts of imperial favor—men of standing regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his father had left the directorship of the Imperial Clan Court to serve as prefect of Huazhou, and father and son simultaneously received edicts of imperial favor—a distinction that men of standing greatly admired.

sentences.zh: ，子婿蘇巢於錢徽下進士及第，其年，巢覆落。

translations.literal: His son-in-law Su Chao passed the jinshi examination under Qian Hui's list. That year, Chao was struck from the rolls upon re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law Su Chao passed the jinshi examination under Qian Hui's examination list, but that same year Chao was struck from the rolls when the results were re-examined.

sentences.zh: 宗閔涉請托，貶劍州刺史。

translations.literal: Zongmin was implicated in solicitations and was demoted to prefect of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin was implicated in improper solicitations and was demoted to prefect of Jian.

sentences.zh: 時李吉甫子德裕為翰林學士，錢徽榜出，德裕與同職李紳、元稹連衡言於上前，雲徽受請托，所試不公，故致重覆。

translations.literal: At the time Li Jifu's son Deyu was a Hanlin academician. When Qian Hui's list was published, Deyu together with his colleagues Li Shen and Yuan Zhen allied to speak before the emperor, saying that Hui had accepted solicitations and the examination was unjust, which led to the re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Jifu's son Deyu was a Hanlin academician. When Qian Hui's examination list was published, Deyu allied with his colleagues Li Shen and Yuan Zhen to speak before the emperor, charging that Hui had accepted solicitations and that the examination had been unfair, which led to the re-examination.

sentences.zh: 比相嫌惡，因是列為朋黨，皆挾邪取權，兩相傾軋。

translations.literal: Because the two sides hated each other, they were henceforth listed as partisan cliques, each taking up perverse means to seize power and mutually tearing one another down.
translations.idiomatic: Because the two sides came to hate each other, they were henceforth treated as rival partisan cliques, each resorting to corrupt means to seize power and striving to destroy the other.

sentences.zh: 自是紛紜排陷，垂四十年。

translations.literal: From then on, contentious purges and entrapments continued for nearly forty years.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, factional purges and entrapments continued for nearly forty years.

sentences.zh: 復入為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He returned to court as Vice Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as vice director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，權知禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year, he served concurrently as acting Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year, he served concurrently as acting vice director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四年，貢舉事畢，權知兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, after the tribute-examination business was finished, he served concurrently as acting Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after the tribute-examination duties were finished, he served concurrently as acting vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: ，正拜兵部侍郎，父憂免。

translations.literal: He was formally appointed Vice Minister of War and was excused from office due to mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was formally appointed vice minister of war, then left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: ，起為吏部侍郎，賜金紫之服。

translations.literal: After mourning he was recalled as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel and was granted the gold-and-purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was recalled as vice director in the Ministry of Personnel and was granted the gold-and-purple robes of high office.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，以本官同平章事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, with his existing rank he became Co-Manager of Affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year, while retaining his existing rank, he became co-manager of affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時裴度薦李德裕，將大用。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Du recommended Li Deyu and intended to employ him in a major role.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Du recommended Li Deyu and intended to give him a major appointment.

sentences.zh: 德裕自浙西入朝，為中人助宗閔者所沮，復出鎮。

translations.literal: Deyu entered court from Zhexi, but was obstructed by those eunuchs who helped Zongmin, and was sent out again to govern a circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu entered court from Zhexi, but was blocked by eunuchs who supported Zongmin and was sent out again to govern a circuit.

sentences.zh: 尋引牛僧孺同知政事，二人唱和，凡德裕之黨皆逐之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zongmin brought in Niu Sengru to share in governing affairs. The two worked in concert, and all members of Deyu's faction were driven away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zongmin brought in Niu Sengru to share in governing affairs. Working in concert, the two drove away everyone in Deyu's faction.

sentences.zh: 累轉中書侍郎、集賢大學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to vice director of the Secretariat and grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 七年，德裕作相。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Deyu became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Deyu became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 六月，罷宗閔知政事，檢校禮部尚書、同平章事、興元尹、山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zongmin was removed from governing affairs and was appointed concurrently as Minister of Rites, Co-Manager of Affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery, Prefect of Xingyuan, and military governor of the Shanan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Zongmin was removed from governing affairs and was appointed concurrently as minister of rites, co-manager of affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery, prefect of Xingyuan, and military governor of the Shanan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 宗閔為吏部侍郎時，因駙馬都尉沈結托女學士宋若憲及知樞密楊承和，二人數稱之於上前，故獲徵用。

translations.literal: When Zongmin was Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, through the efforts of the imperial son-in-law Shen Jietuo, the female academician Song Ruoxian, and the privy-council director Yang Chenghe, the two repeatedly praised him before the emperor, and so he obtained appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongmin was vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, he gained appointment through the imperial son-in-law Shen Jietuo, the female academician Song Ruoxian, and the privy-council director Yang Chenghe, who repeatedly praised him before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及德裕秉政，群邪不悅，而鄭註、李訓深惡之。

translations.literal: When Deyu took power, the corrupt were displeased, and Zheng Zhu and Li Xun deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyu took power, the corrupt were displeased, while Zheng Zhu and Li Xun deeply hated him.

sentences.zh: 文宗乃復召宗閔於興元，為中書侍郎、平章事，命德裕代宗閔為興元尹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong then recalled Zongmin from Xingyuan and appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat and Manager of Affairs, ordering Deyu to replace Zongmin as Prefect of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong then recalled Zongmin from Xingyuan, appointing him vice director of the Secretariat and manager of affairs, and ordered Deyu to replace Zongmin as prefect of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 既再得權位，輔之以訓、註，尤恣所欲，進封襄武侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Once he had regained power, aided by Xun and Zhu, he indulged his desires all the more. He was advanced to Marquis of Xiangwu with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had regained power, aided by Li Xun and Zheng Zhu, he indulged his desires all the more. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangwu with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 九年六月，京兆尹楊虞卿得罪，宗閔極言救解，文宗怒叱之曰：「爾嘗謂鄭覃是妖氣，今作妖，覃耶、爾耶？

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year, when Metropolitan Prefect Yang Yuqing offended, Zongmin spoke at length to plead for him. Emperor Wenzong angrily rebuked him, saying, "You once said that Zheng Tan was an evil influence. Now who is working evil—Tan, or you?"
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year, when Metropolitan Prefect Yang Yuqing fell afoul of the court, Zongmin spoke at length in his defense. Emperor Wenzong angrily rebuked him, saying, "You once said that Zheng Tan was an evil influence. Now who is working evil—Tan, or you?"

sentences.zh: 」翌日，貶明州刺史，尋再貶處州長史。

translations.literal: The next day Zongmin was demoted to prefect of Ming, and soon afterward was demoted again to chief administrator of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zongmin was demoted to prefect of Ming, and soon afterward was demoted again to chief administrator of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 七月，鄭註發沈、宋若憲事，內官楊承和、韋元素、沈及若憲姻黨坐貶者十餘人，又貶宗閔潮州司戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Zheng Zhu exposed the affair of Shen and Song Ruoxian. More than ten inner-court officials, including Yang Chenghe, Wei Yuansu, Shen, and Ruoxian's relatives by marriage, were demoted on account of it, and Zongmin was demoted again to Registrar of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Zheng Zhu exposed the affair involving Shen and Song Ruoxian. More than ten inner-court officials, including Yang Chenghe, Wei Yuansu, Shen, and Ruoxian's relatives by marriage, were demoted on account of it, and Zongmin was demoted again to registrar of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 時訓、註竊弄威權，凡不附己者，目為宗閔、德裕之黨，貶逐無虛日，中外震駭，連月陰晦，人情不安。

translations.literal: At the time Xun and Zhu usurped authority. Whoever did not attach himself to them was labeled a partisan of Zongmin or Deyu, and demotions and banishments came day after day without pause. Inside and outside the court were shaken with alarm; for months on end the skies were overcast, and the people's hearts were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Xun and Zheng Zhu usurped authority. Anyone who did not side with them was labeled a partisan of Zongmin or Deyu, and demotions and banishments came day after day without pause. Court and country alike were shaken with alarm; for months the skies stayed overcast, and public sentiment grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 九月詔曰：

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict declared:

sentences.zh: 朕承天纘歷，燭理不明，勞虛襟以求賢，勵寬德以容眾。

translations.literal: We have received Heaven's mandate and succeeded to the throne, yet Our illumination of governance has not been clear. We have opened Our heart to seek the worthy and cultivated broad virtue to embrace the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: We have received Heaven's mandate and succeeded to the throne, yet Our understanding of governance has not been clear enough. We have opened Our heart to seek the worthy and cultivated broad virtue to embrace the multitude.

sentences.zh: 頃者，或臺輔乖弼違之道，而具僚扇朋附之風；

translations.literal: Recently, some chief ministers have departed from the way of assisting and correcting, while the assembled officials have fanned the wind of partisan attachment;
translations.idiomatic: Recently, some chief ministers have departed from the way of assisting and correcting the throne, while assembled officials have fanned the wind of partisan attachment;

sentences.zh: 翕然相從，實篸彜憲。

translations.literal: they have flocked together in mutual adherence, truly piercing the great norms and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: they have flocked together in mutual adherence, truly piercing the great norms and statutes of governance.

sentences.zh: 致使薰蕕共器，賢不肖並馳；

translations.literal: This has caused fragrant and foul to share the same vessel, and the worthy and unworthy to run side by side;
translations.idiomatic: This has caused the worthy and the unworthy to share the same vessel and to advance side by side;

sentences.zh: 退跡者成後時之夫，登門者有迎吠之客。

translations.literal: those who withdrew became men left behind by the times, while those who came to the gate found guests who barked in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: those who withdrew became men left behind by the times, while those who came to the gate found only fawning partisans.

sentences.zh: 繆戾之氣，堙郁和平，而望陰陽順時，疵癘不作；

translations.literal: Wayward and perverse airs have choked off harmony, yet We still expect yin and yang to follow their seasons and pestilence not to arise;
translations.idiomatic: Wayward and perverse influences have choked off harmony, yet We still expect yin and yang to follow their seasons and pestilence not to arise;

sentences.zh: 朝廷清肅，班列和安，自古及今，未嘗有也。

translations.literal: the court to be pure and solemn, and the ranks to be harmonious and secure—from antiquity to the present, there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: the court to be pure and solemn, and the ranks to be harmonious and secure—from antiquity to the present, there has never been such a thing.

sentences.zh: 今既再申朝典，一變澆風，掃清朋比之徒，匡飭貞廉之俗。

translations.literal: Now We have again proclaimed the court's canonical standards, wholly changed the corrupt wind, swept away partisan cliques, and restored the custom of integrity and probity.
translations.idiomatic: Now We have again proclaimed the court's canonical standards, wholly changed the corrupt wind, swept away partisan cliques, and restored the custom of integrity and probity.

sentences.zh: 凡百卿士，惟新令猷。

translations.literal: Let all you ministers and officials renew your good plans.
translations.idiomatic: Let all you ministers and officials renew your good counsel.

sentences.zh: 如聞周行之中，尚蓄疑懼，或有妄相指目，令不自安，今斯曠然，明喻朕意。

translations.literal: We have heard that among the court ranks there still linger suspicion and fear, and that some recklessly point fingers at one another, leaving others ill at ease. Now We make this clear and openly explain Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that among the court ranks suspicion and fear still linger, and that some recklessly point fingers at one another, leaving others ill at ease. Now We make this clear and openly explain Our intent.

sentences.zh: 應與宗閔、德裕或親或故及門生舊吏等，除今日已前黜遠之外，一切不問。

translations.literal: All who are related to Zongmin or Deyu by kinship or old acquaintance, as well as their students and former subordinates, apart from those already banished before today, shall altogether go unquestioned.
translations.idiomatic: All who are related to Zongmin or Deyu by kinship or old acquaintance, as well as their students and former subordinates, apart from those already banished before today, shall altogether go unquestioned.

sentences.zh: 各安職業，勿復為嫌。

translations.literal: Each shall rest secure in his office and no longer harbor grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Each shall rest secure in his office and no longer harbor grievances against one another.

sentences.zh: 文宗以二李朋黨，繩之不能去，嘗謂侍臣曰：「去河北賊非難，去此朋黨實難。

translations.literal: Because of the partisan cliques of the two Lis, Emperor Wenzong could not remove them even when he tried to restrain them. He once said to his attending ministers, "Removing the rebels of Hebei is not hard; removing these partisan cliques is truly hard."
translations.idiomatic: Because of the partisan cliques of the two Lis, Emperor Wenzong could not remove them even when he tried to restrain them. He once told his attending ministers, "Removing the rebels of Hebei is not hard; removing these partisan cliques is truly hard."

sentences.zh: 」宗閔雖驟放黜，竟免李訓之禍。

translations.literal: Although Zongmin was suddenly dismissed and banished, he ultimately escaped the disaster of Li Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Although Zongmin was suddenly dismissed and banished, he ultimately escaped the disaster brought by Li Xun.

sentences.zh: ，量移衢州司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred by graded demotion to Assistant Administrator of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred by graded demotion to assistant administrator of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，楊嗣復輔政，與宗閔厚善，欲拔用之，而畏鄭覃沮議，乃托中人密諷於上。

translations.literal: In the third year, Yang Sifu assisted in governance. He was on close terms with Zongmin and wished to promote him, but feared that Zheng Tan would block the proposal, so he had a eunuch secretly hint at it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Yang Sifu assisted in governance. He was on close terms with Zongmin and wished to promote him, but feared that Zheng Tan would block the proposal, so he had a eunuch secretly hint at it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上以嗣復故，因紫宸對，謂宰相曰：「宗閔在外四五年，宜別授一官。

translations.literal: Because of Sifu, during an audience in the Zichen Hall the emperor said to the chief ministers, "Zongmin has been outside the court for four or five years. He should be given another office."
translations.idiomatic: Because of Sifu, during an audience in the Zichen Hall the emperor said to the chief ministers, "Zongmin has been outside the court for four or five years. He should be given another office."

sentences.zh: 」鄭覃曰：「陛下憐其地遠，宜移近內地三五百里，不可再用奸邪。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said, "If Your Majesty pities him for being so far away, he should be moved to within three or five hundred li of the inner regions. One must not employ the wicked again."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "If Your Majesty pities him for being so far away, he should be moved to within three or five hundred li of the inner regions. One must not employ the wicked again."

sentences.zh: 陛下若欲用宗閔，臣請先退。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to employ Zongmin, I ask first to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to employ Zongmin, I ask first to withdraw from office.

sentences.zh: 」陳夷行曰：「比者，宗閔得罪，以朋黨之故，恕死為幸。

translations.literal: Chen Yixing said, "Recently Zongmin offended because of partisan cliques. It was good fortune enough that he was spared death."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing said, "Recently Zongmin offended because of partisan cliques. It was good fortune enough that he was spared death."

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，李續之、張又新、蘇景胤等，朋比奸險，幾傾朝廷，時號『八關十六子』。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoli reign, Li Xuzhi, Zhang Youxin, Su Jingyin, and others formed a corrupt and treacherous clique that nearly overturned the court. At the time they were called the "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoli reign, Li Xuzhi, Zhang Youxin, Su Jingyin, and others formed a corrupt and treacherous clique that nearly overturned the court. At the time they were called the "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."

sentences.zh: 」李玨曰：「主此事者，罪在逢吉。

translations.literal: Li Jue said, "The one chiefly responsible for this affair was Fengji."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said, "The one chiefly responsible for this affair was Fengji."

sentences.zh: 李續之居喪服闋，不可不與一官，臣恐中外衣冠，交興議論，非為續之輩也。

translations.literal: Li Xuzhi has completed mourning and cannot be denied some office. I fear that officials inside and outside the court will all begin to talk about it—not for the sake of Xuzhi and his like alone.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuzhi has completed mourning and cannot be denied some office. I fear that officials inside and outside the court will all begin to talk about it—not for the sake of Xuzhi and his like alone.

sentences.zh: 」夷行曰：「昔舜逐四兇天下治。

translations.literal: Yixing said, "In antiquity, when Shun drove out the Four Evils, the realm was governed."
translations.idiomatic: Yixing said, "In antiquity, when Shun drove out the Four Evils, the realm was well governed."

sentences.zh: 朝廷求理，何惜此十數纖人？

translations.literal: If the court seeks good order, why spare these dozen or so petty men?
translations.idiomatic: If the court seeks good order, why spare these dozen or so petty men?

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「事貴得中，不可但徇憎愛。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "Affairs must strike the mean; one cannot simply follow hatred or favor alone."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "Affairs must strike the mean; one cannot simply follow personal hatred or favor alone."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「與一郡可也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Giving him a prefecture would be acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Giving him a prefecture would be acceptable."

sentences.zh: 」鄭覃曰：「與郡太優，止可洪州司馬耳。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said, "A prefecture is too generous. He should receive only the post of Assistant Administrator of Hongzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "A prefecture is too generous. He should receive only the post of assistant administrator of Hongzhou."

sentences.zh: 」夷行曰：「宗閔養成鄭註之惡，幾覆邦家，國之巨蠹也。

translations.literal: Yixing said, "Zongmin nurtured the evil of Zheng Zhu and nearly overturned the state. He is a great bane to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Yixing said, "Zongmin nurtured the evil of Zheng Zhu and nearly overturned the state. He is a great bane to the realm."

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「比者，陛下欲加鄭註官，宗閔不肯，陛下亦當記憶。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "Recently, when Your Majesty wished to promote Zheng Zhu, Zongmin refused to agree. Your Majesty should remember that as well."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "Recently, when Your Majesty wished to promote Zheng Zhu, Zongmin refused to agree. Your Majesty should remember that as well."

sentences.zh: 」覃曰：「嗣復黨庇宗閔。

translations.literal: Tan said, "Sifu is shielding Zongmin as a partisan."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "Sifu is shielding Zongmin as a partisan."

sentences.zh: 臣觀宗閔之惡，甚於李林甫。

translations.literal: In my view, Zongmin's wickedness surpasses that of Li Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, Zongmin's wickedness surpasses that of Li Linfu.

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「覃語大過。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "Tan's words go too far."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "Tan's words go too far."

sentences.zh: 昔玄宗季年，委用林甫，妒賢害能，破人家族。

translations.literal: In the late years of Emperor Xuanzong, he entrusted power to Linfu, who envied the worthy, harmed the capable, and destroyed families.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of Emperor Xuanzong, he entrusted power to Linfu, who envied the worthy, harmed the capable, and destroyed families.

sentences.zh: 宗閔在位，固無此事。

translations.literal: When Zongmin held office, there was certainly nothing of that sort.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongmin held office, there was certainly nothing of that sort.

sentences.zh: 況太和末，宗閔、德裕同時得罪。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the end of the Taihe reign, Zongmin and Deyu both offended at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at the end of the Taihe reign, Zongmin and Deyu both offended at the same time.

sentences.zh: 二年之間，德裕再領重鎮，而宗閔未離貶所。

translations.literal: Within two years, Deyu twice took command of major circuits, while Zongmin had not yet left his place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years, Deyu twice took command of major circuits, while Zongmin had not yet left his place of banishment.

sentences.zh: 陛下懲惡勸善，進退之理宜均，非臣獨敢黨庇。

translations.literal: Your Majesty punishes evil and encourages good. The principle of advancement and withdrawal should be even-handed. It is not that I alone dare to shield a partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty punishes evil and encourages good. The principle of advancement and withdrawal should be even-handed. It is not that I alone dare to shield a partisan.

sentences.zh: 昨殷侑與韓益奏官及章服，臣以益前年犯贓，未可其奏；

translations.literal: Yesterday Yin You and Han Yi memorialized about office and ceremonial robes. I held that Yi had committed embezzlement the year before last and could not approve their memorial;
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday Yin You and Han Yi memorialized about office and ceremonial robes. I held that Yi had committed embezzlement the year before last and could not approve their memorial;

sentences.zh: 鄭覃托臣雲『幸且勿論。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan asked me, saying, "For now, please do not press the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan asked me, saying, "For now, please do not press the matter."

sentences.zh: 』孰為黨庇？

translations.literal: Who then is shielding a partisan?
translations.idiomatic: Who then is shielding a partisan?

sentences.zh: 」翌日，以宗閔為杭州刺史。

translations.literal: The next day, Zongmin was appointed prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, Zongmin was appointed prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，遷太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year, he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent and served at the Eastern Capital in a nominal post.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year, he was transferred to mentor of the heir apparent and served at the Eastern Capital in a nominal post.

sentences.zh: 時鄭覃、陳夷行罷相，嗣復方再拔用宗閔知政事，俄而文宗崩。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Tan and Chen Yixing had been removed as chief ministers, and Sifu was just about to promote Zongmin again to share in governing affairs when Emperor Wenzong suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zheng Tan and Chen Yixing had been removed as chief ministers, and Sifu was just about to promote Zongmin again to share in governing affairs when Emperor Wenzong suddenly died.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，李德裕秉政，嗣復、李玨皆竄嶺表。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huichang reign, when Li Deyu took power, Sifu and Li Jue were both banished to the regions south of the Ling Range.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huichang reign, when Li Deyu took power, Sifu and Li Jue were both banished to the regions south of the Ling Range.

sentences.zh: 三年，劉稹據澤潞叛。

translations.literal: In the third year, Liu Zhen held Ze and Lu and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Liu Zhen seized Ze and Lu and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 德裕以宗閔素與劉從諫厚，上黨近東都，宗閔分司非便，出為封州刺史。

translations.literal: Deyu, because Zongmin had long been on close terms with Liu Congjian, and because Shangdang was near the Eastern Capital, held that it was unsuitable for Zongmin to serve there in a nominal post. Zongmin was sent out as prefect of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu, because Zongmin had long been on close terms with Liu Congjian and because Shangdang was near the Eastern Capital, held that it was unsuitable for Zongmin to serve there in a nominal post, and sent him out as prefect of Feng.

sentences.zh: 又發其舊事，貶郴州司馬，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: Deyu also exposed his old offenses, and Zongmin was demoted to Assistant Administrator of Chen. He died in his place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu also exposed his old offenses, and Zongmin was demoted to assistant administrator of Chen. He died in his place of banishment.

sentences.zh: 子琨、瓚，大中朝皆進士擢第。

translations.literal: His sons Kun and Zan both passed the jinshi examination during the Dazhong reign.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Kun and Zan both passed the jinshi examination during the Dazhong reign.

sentences.zh: 令狐綯作相，特加獎拔。

translations.literal: When Linghu Tao became chief minister, he gave them special encouragement and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Tao became chief minister, he gave them special encouragement and promotion.

sentences.zh: 瓚自員外郎知制誥，歷中書舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: Zan, starting from Vice Director, was put in charge of drafting edicts, and served in succession as Vice Director in the Secretariat and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Zan, starting as a vice director, was put in charge of drafting edicts and served in succession as vice director in the Secretariat and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 綯罷相，出為桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: When Tao was removed as chief minister, Zan was sent out as observation commissioner of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao was removed as chief minister, Zan was sent out as observation commissioner of Gui.

sentences.zh: 御軍無政，為卒所逐，貶死。

translations.literal: He governed the army without proper discipline, was driven out by his soldiers, and died in demotion.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the army without proper discipline, was driven out by his soldiers, and died in exile after demotion.

sentences.zh: 自天寶艱難之後，宗室子弟，賢而立功者，唯鄭王、曹王子孫耳。

translations.literal: After the hardships of the Tianbao era, among the sons and younger kinsmen of the imperial clan who were worthy and established merit, there were only the descendants of the Princes of Zheng and Cao.
translations.idiomatic: After the hardships of the Tianbao era, among the sons and younger kinsmen of the imperial clan who were worthy and established merit, there were only the descendants of the Princes of Zheng and Cao.

sentences.zh: 夷簡再從季父汧國公勉，德宗朝宰相。

translations.literal: Yijian's second cousin once removed was the Prince of Qian, Gong Mian, a chief minister in the reign of Emperor Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian's second cousin once removed was Prince Qian, Gong Mian, who had served as chief minister under Emperor Dezong.

sentences.zh: 夷簡諸弟夷亮、夷則、夷範，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: Yi Jian's younger brothers Yi Liang, Yi Ze, and Yi Fan all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Jian's younger brothers Yi Liang, Yi Ze, and Yi Fan all attained jinshi rank.

sentences.zh: 宗閔弟宗冉。

translations.literal: Zongmin's younger brother was Zong Ran.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin's younger brother was Zong Ran.

sentences.zh: 宗冉子深、湯。

translations.literal: Zong Ran had sons Shen and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ran's sons were Shen and Tang.

sentences.zh: 湯累官至給事中，咸通中踐更臺閣，知名於時。

translations.literal: Tang rose through successive offices to Supervising Secretary; during the Xiantong reign he served in various posts within the central administration and was renowned in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Tang eventually reached the post of Supervising Secretary; under the Xiantong emperor he rotated through offices in the capital secretariat and won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣復楊嗣復，字繼之，僕射於陵子也。

translations.literal: Yang Sifu, whose courtesy name was Jizhi, was the son of Grand Counselor Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sifu (zi Jizhi) was the son of Grand Counselor Yang Yuling.

sentences.zh: 初，於陵十九登進十第，二十再登博學宏詞科，謂補潤州句容尉。

translations.literal: At first, at nineteen Yuling passed the jinshi examination; at twenty he passed again in the Examination for Erudite Learning and Lofty Literary Expression, and was assigned as assistant magistrate of Jurong in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Yang Yuling passed the jinshi at nineteen and the boxue hongci examination at twenty, then received appointment as assistant magistrate of Jurong in Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使韓滉有知人之鑒，見之甚悅。

translations.literal: Han Huang, the Zhexi Observation Commissioner, had a keen eye for judging men; upon meeting him he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, Commissioner of the Zhexi Circuit, was famed for discerning men's true worth, and was deeply impressed when he met Yang Yuling.

sentences.zh: 滉有愛女，方擇佳婿，謂其妻柳氏曰：「吾閱人多矣，無如楊生貴而有壽，生子必為宰相。

translations.literal: Han Huang had a beloved daughter and was choosing a fine son-in-law; he said to his wife, Lady Liu: "I have reviewed many men, and none compare with Young Yang—noble in bearing and long-lived; the sons he begets will surely become chancellors."
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang had a cherished daughter and was seeking a worthy match; he told his wife Lady Liu, "I have seen countless men, yet none like young Yang—of noble mien and destined for long life; sons born to him will surely reach the chancellorship."

sentences.zh: 」於陵秩滿，寓居揚州而生嗣復。

translations.literal: When Yuling's term of office ended, he took up residence in Yangzhou, and there Sifu was born.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuling's term expired he settled in Yangzhou, and there Yang Sifu was born.

sentences.zh: 後滉見之，撫其首曰：「名位果逾於父，楊門之慶也。

translations.literal: Later, when Han Huang saw him, he stroked his head and said, "Your fame and rank have indeed surpassed your father's—the joy of the Yang house."
translations.idiomatic: Later Han Huang met the boy, stroked his head, and said, "Your name and station will indeed exceed your father's—a blessing upon the house of Yang."

sentences.zh: 」因字曰慶門。

translations.literal: Accordingly he gave him the courtesy name Qingmen.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore bestowed upon him the courtesy name Qingmen, "Celebration Gate."

sentences.zh: 嗣復七八歲時已能秉筆為文。

translations.literal: When Sifu was seven or eight years old he could already take up the brush and compose essays.
translations.idiomatic: By the age of seven or eight Sifu could already wield the brush and write compositions.

sentences.zh: 年二十，進士擢第。

translations.literal: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 二十一，又登博學宏詞科，釋褐秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: At twenty-one he passed again in the Examination for Erudite Learning and Lofty Literary Expression, and upon leaving his rough clothes took office as collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-one he passed the boxue hongci examination and, upon donning official robes, was appointed collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷右拾遺，直史館。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Reminder and served on duty in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Reminder and assigned to duty in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 以嗣復深於禮學，改太常博士。

translations.literal: Because Sifu was deeply versed in ritual learning, he was reassigned as Erudite of the Grand Ritual Office.
translations.idiomatic: On account of Sifu's deep mastery of ritual studies, he was transferred to the post of Erudite in the Grand Ritual Office.

sentences.zh: ，累遷至刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached the post of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 鄭餘慶為詳定禮儀使，奏為判官，改禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuqing, as Commissioner for Determining Ritual Protocols, memorialized to appoint him as his administrative aide; he was reassigned as Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yuqing served as Commissioner for Determining Ritual Protocols, he recommended Sifu as his aide and had him transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時父於陵為戶部侍郎，嗣復上言與父同省非便，請換他官。

translations.literal: At that time his father Yuling was Vice Minister of Revenue; Sifu submitted a memorial saying that serving with his father in the same ministry was inconvenient and asked to be transferred to another office.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his father Yuling was Vice Minister of Revenue; Sifu memorialized the throne that serving alongside his father in the same ministry was unseemly and requested transfer elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「應同司官有大功以下親者，但非連判及勾檢之官並官長，則不在回避之限。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "For officials of the same department who have relatives within the degree of great merit and below, so long as they are not consecutive judges or audit-and-inspection officers, nor heads of the office, they are not within the limits of avoidance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied by edict: "When officials of one department share kinship within the degree of great merit or closer, they need not withdraw unless they serve as consecutive judges, audit officers, or department heads—those cases fall outside the rule of avoidance."

sentences.zh: 如官署同，職司異，雖父子兄弟無所避嫌。

translations.literal: If the office is the same but the duties differ, even father and son or brothers need not avoid suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: When the department is shared but the duties differ, even fathers and sons or brothers need not shun one another.

sentences.zh: 」再遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Bureau Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十月，以庫部郎中知制誥，正拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he served as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Stores with concurrent duty drafting edicts, and was formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, while serving as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Stores he was charged with drafting edicts, and was formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 嗣復與牛僧孺、李宗閔皆權德輿貢舉門生，情義相得，進退取舍，多與之同。

translations.literal: Sifu, together with Niu Sengru and Li Zongmin, were all examination disciples of Quan Deyu; they were bound in mutual affection, and in advancement, withdrawal, and choice of action they largely acted in accord with one another.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu, Niu Sengru, and Li Zongmin had all been examination disciples of Quan Deyu; united in friendship, they largely moved together in office—advancing, withdrawing, and choosing sides as one.

sentences.zh: 四年，僧孺作相，欲薦拔大用，又以於陵為東都留守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Sengru became chancellor and wished to recommend Sifu for great advancement; moreover Yuling was Eastern Capital Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Niu Sengru took the chancellorship and sought to elevate Sifu to high office; meanwhile Yuling served as Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 未歷相位，乃令嗣復權知禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Not having yet served in the chancellorship himself, Sengru had Sifu act as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before Sengru himself had held the chancellorship, he had Sifu serve as acting Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二月，選貢士六十八人，後多至達官。

translations.literal: In the second month he selected sixty-eight tribute scholars, many of whom later reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he selected sixty-eight tribute scholars, many of whom later rose to eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, Sifu was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne, Sifu was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以父於陵太子少傅致仕，年高多疾，懇辭侍養，不之許。

translations.literal: Because his father Yuling had retired as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and, being advanced in years, suffered many illnesses, Sifu earnestly begged leave to remain home and serve him, but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Yuling retired as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, aged and often ill, Sifu pleaded earnestly to withdraw and tend him at home, but the throne would not allow it.

sentences.zh: ，丁父憂免。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he entered mourning and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He then mourned his father's death and left office.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，起為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year he was recalled to serve as Left Vice Director of the Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year he was recalled as Left Vice Director of the Ministries.

sentences.zh: 其年宗閔罷相，德裕輔政。

translations.literal: That year Li Zongmin was removed from the chancellorship and Li Deyu assisted in governing.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Zongmin left the chancellorship and Li Deyu took up the reins of government.

sentences.zh: 七月，以嗣復檢校禮部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Sifu was made provisional Minister of Rites, Prefect of Zizhou, and Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Jiannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Sifu was appointed provisional Minister of Rites, Prefect of Zizhou, and Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of the Jiannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 九年，宗閔復知政事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Li Zongmin again took charge of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Li Zongmin returned to direct the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 三月，以嗣復檢校戶部尚書、成都尹、劍南西川節度副大使知節度事、觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the third month Sifu was made provisional Minister of Revenue, Governor of Chengdu, Deputy Military Governor of Jiannan West Circuit with authority over military affairs, and Commissioner for Observation and Disposition.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Sifu was appointed provisional Minister of Revenue, Governor of Chengdu, and Deputy Military Governor of the Jiannan West Circuit with full authority over the command and its observation affairs.

sentences.zh: 十月，入為戶部侍郎，領諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Revenue and head of the Salt and Iron Transport Commission for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he returned to court as Vice Minister of Revenue and Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，與同列李玨並以本官同平章事，領使如故，進階金紫，弘農伯，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he and his colleague Li Jue were both appointed Co-Chancellors while retaining their original posts and commissions; he was advanced to golden-purple rank, enfeoffed as Marquis of Hongnong, with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he and his colleague Li Jue were both made Co-Chancellors while keeping their existing offices and commissions; Sifu was raised to golden-purple rank, enfeoffed as Marquis of Hongnong with seven hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 上以幣輕錢重，問鹽鐵使何以去其太甚？

translations.literal: Because coins were light and cash heavy, the emperor asked the Salt and Iron Commissioner how to remove the excess.
translations.idiomatic: Observing that coin was debased while cash grew scarce, the emperor asked the Salt and Iron Commissioner how the worst of the imbalance might be remedied.

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「此事累朝制置未得，但且禁銅，未可變法。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "This matter has gone unresolved through successive reigns; for the present we should merely forbid copper, and must not yet change the law."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu replied, "Successive courts have failed to settle this; for now we should enforce the ban on copper and not rashly alter the law."

sentences.zh: 法變擾人，終亦未罷去弊。

translations.literal: When laws are changed they disturb the people, and in the end the abuses are still not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Alter the law and you trouble the people, yet the evil is not finally removed.

sentences.zh: 」李玨曰：「禁銅之令，朝廷常典，但行之不嚴，不如無令。

translations.literal: Li Jue said, "The ban on copper is a standing statute of the court, but if it is not enforced strictly, it would be better to have no statute at all."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said, "The prohibition on copper is long-established court law—but a law loosely enforced might as well not exist."

sentences.zh: 今江淮已南，銅器成肆，市井逐利者，銷錢一緡，可為數器，售利三四倍。

translations.literal: Now south of the Yangtze and Huai, shops of copper vessels fill the markets; profiteers in the towns melt cash—one string of coins can be made into several vessels, yielding three or four times the profit.
translations.idiomatic: Today south of the Yangtze and Huai, copperware shops line the markets; townsmen chasing profit melt coin by the string into several vessels and sell them for three- or fourfold gain.

sentences.zh: 遠民不知法令，率以為常。

translations.literal: Common people in distant regions do not know the statutes and generally treat this as normal.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants in remote districts, ignorant of the law, take this for ordinary practice.

sentences.zh: 縱國家加爐鑄錢，何以供銷鑄之弊？

translations.literal: Even if the state adds furnaces to cast coin, how can it supply the drain of melting and casting?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the state poured more furnaces into minting, how could it keep pace with the coin lost to illicit melting?

sentences.zh: 所以禁銅之令，不得不嚴。

translations.literal: Therefore the ban on copper cannot but be enforced strictly.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the ban on copper must be enforced without laxity.

sentences.zh: 八月，紫宸奏事，曰：「聖人在上，野無遺賢。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, reporting affairs in the Purple Hall, he said, "When a sage is upon the throne, no worthy man is left in the wilds."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, speaking in the Purple Hall, he said, "Under a sage ruler no talent languishes in obscurity."

sentences.zh: 陸洿上疏論兵，雖不中時事，意亦可獎。

translations.literal: Lu Yu submitted a memorial discussing military affairs; though it did not fit the times, the intention is still worthy of reward.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu had memorialized on military matters; though untimely, his purpose deserved commendation.

sentences.zh: 閑居蘇州累年，宜與一官。

translations.literal: He has lived in retirement in Suzhou for many years and should be given an office.
translations.idiomatic: Having lived in seclusion at Suzhou for many years, he should be granted a post.

sentences.zh: 」李玨曰：「士子趨競者多，若獎陸洿，貪夫知勸矣。

translations.literal: Li Jue said, "Many scholars rush in competition; if Lu Yu is rewarded, the greedy will know encouragement."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said, "Too many scholars scramble for favor; reward Lu Yu and the covetous will take it as invitation."

sentences.zh: 昨竇洵直論事，陛下賞之以幣帛，況與陸洿官耶？

translations.literal: Yesterday Dou Xunzhi spoke on affairs of state and Your Majesty rewarded him with silks and cloth—how much more so for giving Lu Yu an office?
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday Dou Xunzhi spoke forth on policy and Your Majesty rewarded him with silks—would you now grant Lu Yu an office as well?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「洵直獎其直心，不言事之當否。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Xunzhi was rewarded for his forthrightness of heart, not for whether his words were right or wrong."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I rewarded Xunzhi for the honesty of his heart, not for the correctness of his counsel."

sentences.zh: 」鄭覃曰：「若苞藏則不可知。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said, "If one harbors hidden designs, that cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "When men conceal their true intent, who can discern it?"

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「臣深知洵直無邪惡，所奏陸洿官，尚未奉聖旨。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "Your servant knows well that Xunzhi has no wickedness; as for the office for Lu Yu that I memorialized, I have not yet received the imperial decree."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "I know Xunzhi to be free of evil design; as for my recommendation of an office for Lu Yu, I have not yet received Your Majesty's command."

sentences.zh: 」鄭覃曰：「陛下須防朋黨。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said, "Your Majesty must guard against factions."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "Your Majesty must beware of cliques."

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「鄭覃疑臣朋黨，乞陛下放臣歸去。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "Zheng Tan suspects your servant of faction; I beg Your Majesty to release me to return home."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "Zheng Tan accuses me of clique-making; I beg Your Majesty to dismiss me and let me go home."

sentences.zh: 」因拜乞罷免。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bowed and begged to be removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed low and pleaded to be relieved of office.

sentences.zh: 李玨曰：「比來朋黨，近亦稍弭。

translations.literal: Li Jue said, "Factional strife of late has somewhat subsided."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said, "The factional quarrels of recent times have already begun to quiet."

sentences.zh: 」覃曰：「近有小朋黨生。

translations.literal: Tan said, "Recently small factions have arisen anew."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "Of late small cliques have sprung up again."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此輩雕喪向盡。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "That crowd's carved mourning is nearly exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That faction is nearly spent—its carved tombs almost full."

sentences.zh: 」覃曰：「楊漢公、張又新、李續之即今尚在。

translations.literal: Tan said, "Yang Hangong, Zhang Youxin, and Li Xuzhi are still alive today."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "Yang Hangong, Zhang Youxin, and Li Xuzhi yet live."

sentences.zh: 」玨曰：「今有邊事論奏。

translations.literal: Jue said, "Today there is memorializing on frontier affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said, "Today the court has frontier business to discuss."

sentences.zh: 」覃曰：「論邊事安危，臣不如玨；

translations.literal: Tan said, "In discussing the safety and peril of frontier affairs, your servant is not the equal of Jue;"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "When it comes to weighing the peril of the frontier, I am no match for Jue;"

sentences.zh: 嫉惡則玨不如臣。

translations.literal: in hating evil, Jue is not the equal of your servant."
translations.idiomatic: but in detesting wickedness, Jue is no match for me."

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「臣聞左右佩劍，彼此相笑。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "Your servant has heard that men wearing swords at their sides laugh at one another."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "I have heard that swordsmen at one another's sides are the first to mock each other's blades."

sentences.zh: 臣今不知鄭覃指誰為朋黨。

translations.literal: Today your servant does not know whom Zheng Tan means as a faction.
translations.idiomatic: Today I do not know whom Zheng Tan has in mind when he speaks of cliques.

sentences.zh: 」因當香案前奏曰：「臣待罪宰相，不能申夔、龍之道，唯以朋黨見譏，必乞陛下罷臣鼎職。

translations.literal: Thereupon, before the incense table, he memorialized, saying, "Your servant, bearing guilt as chancellor, has been unable to proclaim the Way of Kui and Long; accused only of clique-making, I must beg Your Majesty to remove me from the cauldron office."
translations.idiomatic: He then addressed the throne before the incense table: "I stand guilty as chancellor, unable to uphold the sage governance of Kui and Long; reproached solely as a faction-maker, I beg Your Majesty to strip me of this post."

sentences.zh: 」上慰勉之。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soothed and urged him to remain.

sentences.zh: 文宗方以政事委嗣復，惡覃言切。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong was then entrusting governmental affairs to Sifu and disliked Tan's sharp words.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong had already entrusted the governance to Sifu and took offense at Zheng Tan's cutting speech.

sentences.zh: 帝延英謂宰臣曰：「人傳符讖之語，自何而來？

translations.literal: In Yanying Hall the emperor asked the chancellors, "People circulate words of prophecy and omen—whence do they come?"
translations.idiomatic: At Yanying Hall the emperor asked his chancellors, "Prophetic sayings circulate among the people—where do they arise?"

sentences.zh: 」嗣復對曰：「漢光武好以讖書決事，近代隋文帝亦信此言，自是，此說日滋，只如班彪《王命論》所引，蓋矯意以止賊亂，非所重也。

translations.literal: Sifu replied, "Emperor Guangwu of Han loved to decide affairs by apocryphal texts; in recent times Emperor Wen of Sui also believed such words; from then on this doctrine daily grew. Even such passages as Ban Biao's Wangming Lun cites were largely feigned intent to halt rebellion and banditry—not something to be esteemed."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu answered, "Han Guangwu loved to decide policy by apocryphal prophecy; Sui Wendi trusted such talk as well, and from that day the doctrine spread. Even what Ban Biao's Discourse on the Mandate of Kings cites was largely artifice to quell rebellion—not wisdom to be revered."

sentences.zh: 」李玨曰：「喪亂之時，佐命者務神符命；

translations.literal: Li Jue said, "In times of mourning and chaos, those who aid the mandate busy themselves with divine signs and fate;"
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said, "In ages of ruin and upheaval, men who rise to serve the mandate lean upon omens and fate;"

sentences.zh: 理平之代，只合推諸人事。

translations.literal: in an age of order and peace one should rely only upon human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: in an age of peace one should look only to human effort."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You speak rightly."

sentences.zh: 」帝又曰：「天後用人，有自布衣至宰相者，當時還得力否？

translations.literal: The emperor also said, "When the Empress Wu used men, some rose from common cloth to chancellor—were they effective at the time?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also asked, "When Empress Wu raised men from commoners to the chancellorship, did they prove capable?"

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「天後重行刑辟，輕用官爵，皆自圖之計耳。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "The Empress Wu emphasized harsh punishments and lightly bestowed offices and ranks—all schemes of self-interest."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "Empress Wu relied heavily on punishment and lightly on rank—all calculated for her own ends."

sentences.zh: 凡用人之道，歷試方見其能否。

translations.literal: The way of employing men generally requires repeated trial before one sees whether they can or cannot.
translations.idiomatic: The proper way to employ men is to test them through service before judging their capacity.

sentences.zh: 當艱難之時，或須拔擢，無事之日，不如且循資級。

translations.literal: In difficult times one may need sudden promotion; in untroubled days it is better to follow seniority step by step.
translations.idiomatic: In crisis one may need to lift men abruptly; in calm times it is better to advance them by seniority.

sentences.zh: 古人拔卒為將，非治平之時，蓋不獲已而用之也。

translations.literal: The ancients plucked a soldier from the ranks to make a general—not in times of good order; they used such men only when they had no choice."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients made generals of common soldiers—not in tranquil ages, but only when necessity left no other course."

sentences.zh: 」上又問新修《開元政要》，敘致何如。

translations.literal: The emperor further asked about the newly compiled Kaiyuan Zhengyao—how was its narrative arrangement?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor next asked about the newly edited Essentials of Governance from the Kaiyuan Era—what of its arrangement and tone?

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「臣等未見。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "Your servants have not yet seen it."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "We have not yet seen the text."

sentences.zh: 陛下若欲遺之子孫，則請宣付臣等，參詳可否。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to bequeath it to posterity, then please have it transmitted to your servants so that we may examine what may or may not stand.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty means to bequeath it to posterity, let it be sent to us that we may judge what should remain and what should not.

sentences.zh: 玄宗或好遊畋，或好聲色，與貞觀之政不同，故取舍須當，方堪流傳。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong at times loved hunting and at times loved music and women—unlike the governance of the Zhenguan reign; therefore what is kept and what is discarded must be fitting before it can be handed down."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong indulged at times in the hunt and at times in pleasure—far from the governance of the Zhenguan era; what is preserved and what is cut must be chosen with care if the work is to endure."

sentences.zh: 四年五月，上問延英政事，逐日何人記錄監修？

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year the emperor, inquiring about affairs at Yanying Hall, asked who recorded and supervised the daily proceedings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year, questioning policy at Yanying Hall, the emperor asked who kept and oversaw the daily record of court business.

sentences.zh: 李玨曰：「是臣職司。

translations.literal: Li Jue said, "It is your servant's duty."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said, "That falls to me."

sentences.zh: 」陳夷行曰：「宰相所錄，必當自伐，聖德即將掩之。

translations.literal: Chen Yixing said, "What chancellors record must inevitably be self-praise; sagely virtue will soon be obscured."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing said, "When chancellors keep the record they inevitably glorify themselves—and the emperor's true merit will be eclipsed."

sentences.zh: 臣所以頻言，不欲威權在下。

translations.literal: The reason your servant has spoken of this repeatedly is that I do not wish authority to rest below.
translations.idiomatic: I have raised this again and again because I will not see authority lodged below the throne.

sentences.zh: 」玨曰：「夷行此言，是疑宰相中有賣威權、貨刑賞者。

translations.literal: Jue said, "Yixing's words imply suspicion that among the chancellors there are those who sell authority and trade punishments and rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said, "Yixing's remark suggests he suspects some chancellor of peddling power and bartering punishments and rewards."

sentences.zh: 不然，何自為宰相而出此言？

translations.literal: Otherwise, being himself a chancellor, why would he speak thus?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise why, being a chancellor himself, would he say such a thing?

sentences.zh: 臣累奏求退，若得王傅，臣之幸也。

translations.literal: Your servant has repeatedly memorialized asking to retire; if I could obtain the post of Royal Tutor, that would be my good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: I have repeatedly asked to withdraw; if I might become Royal Tutor, I would count myself fortunate.

sentences.zh: 」鄭覃曰：「陛下、二年政事至好，三年、四年漸不如前。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said, "Your Majesty, the governance of the first and second years was excellent; the third and fourth years have gradually fallen short of before."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "Your Majesty, the first two years of your reign went well; the third and fourth have steadily declined."

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「元年、二年是鄭覃、夷行用事，三年、四年臣與李玨同之。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "The first and second years were when Zheng Tan and Yixing held power; the third and fourth years your servant shared governance with Li Jue."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "The first two years belonged to Zheng Tan and Chen Yixing; the third and fourth my colleague Li Jue and I shared."

sentences.zh: 臣蒙聖慈擢處相位，不能悉心奉職。

translations.literal: Your servant, favored by imperial kindness and raised to the chancellorship, has been unable to devote himself fully to duty.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to the chancellorship by your grace, I have failed to serve with my whole heart.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃云『三年之後，一年不如一年』，臣之罪也。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan says, 'After the third year, each year has been worse than the last'—that is your servant's crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Tan says that after the third year each year has grown worse, the fault is mine.

sentences.zh: 陛下縱不誅夷，臣合自求泯滅。

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty does not punish Yixing, your servant ought himself to seek extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty does not punish Yixing, I ought to remove myself from sight.

sentences.zh: 」因叩頭曰：「臣今日便辭玉階，不敢更入中書。

translations.literal: Thereupon, kowtowing, he said, "Your servant today will leave the jade steps and dare not enter the Secretariat again."
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed and said, "Today I quit the jade steps and will not again set foot in the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 」即趨去。

translations.literal: At once he hurried away.
translations.idiomatic: He turned and hastened out.

sentences.zh: 上令中使召還，勞之曰：「鄭覃失言，卿何及此？

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a palace envoy to summon him back and comforted him, saying, "Zheng Tan spoke amiss—why go so far?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to recall him and said gently, "Zheng Tan misspoke—why take it so hard?"

sentences.zh: 」覃起謝曰：「臣性愚拙，言無顧慮。

translations.literal: Tan rose and apologized, saying, "Your servant is dull and clumsy by nature; my words lack forethought."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan rose and apologized: "I am dull by nature and spoke without due care."

sentences.zh: 近日事亦漸好，未免些些不公，亦無甚處。

translations.literal: In recent days affairs have also gradually improved; unavoidably there remain some small injustices, yet there is nothing very serious.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs have lately improved somewhat; minor injustices remain, but nothing of great moment.

sentences.zh: 臣亦不獨斥嗣復，遽何至此。

translations.literal: Your servant also did not single out Sifu alone for censure—why so suddenly reach this point?
translations.idiomatic: I did not censure Sifu alone—why has it come to this so suddenly?

sentences.zh: 所為若是，乃嗣復不容臣耳。

translations.literal: If he acts like this, it is simply that Sifu cannot tolerate your servant.
translations.idiomatic: If he behaves thus, it is because Sifu will not tolerate me.

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「陛下不以臣微才，用為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Sifu said, "Your Majesty, not considering your servant's slight talent, employed me as Vice Director of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Li Sifu said, "Your Majesty, overlooking my modest gifts, appointed me Vice Director of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 時政善否，其責在臣。

translations.literal: Whether current policy is good or ill, the responsibility lies with your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the times are well or ill governed, the burden is mine.

sentences.zh: 陛下月費俸錢數十萬，時新珍異，必先賜與，蓋欲輔佐聖明，臻於至理。

translations.literal: Your Majesty spends several hundred thousand in monthly salary, and seasonal novelties and rarities are always first bestowed upon me—surely meaning to assist sagely clarity and reach the utmost governance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pays me hundreds of thousands each month in salary, and seasonal delicacies and rare gifts are always sent to me first—all so that I may aid Your Majesty in bringing the realm to perfect order.

sentences.zh: 既一年不如一年，非惟臣合得罪，亦上累聖德。

translations.literal: Year after year things have grown worse—not only ought your servant be punished, it also reflects upon Your Majesty's sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Each year has been worse than the last—not only should I be punished, but Your Majesty's own virtue is diminished thereby.

sentences.zh: 伏請別命賢能，許臣休退。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly asks that another capable man be appointed, and that your servant be permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that another worthy be appointed in my place and that I be allowed to withdraw from office.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「鄭覃之言偶然耳，奚執咎耶？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Zheng Tan's words were merely casual—why dwell on the offense?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zheng Tan spoke casually—why take offense?"

sentences.zh: 」嗣復數日不入，上表請罷。

translations.literal: Sifu for several days did not enter court, submitting a memorial requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sifu stayed away from court for several days and submitted a memorial asking to be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 帝方委用，乃罷鄭覃、夷行知政事。

translations.literal: The emperor was just then relying on him, so he dismissed Zheng Tan and Yexing from directing government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then relying on Li Sifu, and dismissed Zheng Tan and Li Yexing from directing the government.

sentences.zh: 自是，政歸嗣復，進加門下侍郎。

translations.literal: From this point, government affairs returned to Sifu, who was promoted and given the additional title of Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: From then on power returned to Li Sifu, who was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，文宗崩。

translations.literal: The first month of the following year, Emperor Wenzong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, Emperor Wenzong died.

sentences.zh: 先是，以敬宗子陳王為皇太子。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Jingzong's son the Prince of Chen had been made crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Jingzong's son, the Prince of Chen, had been named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 中尉仇士良違遺令立武宗。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Right Army Qiu Shiliang violated the deathbed command and enthroned Emperor Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant of the Right Army, Qiu Shiliang, defied the dying emperor's command and enthroned Emperor Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 武宗之立，既非宰相本意，甚薄執政之臣。

translations.literal: Since Wuzong's enthronement was not the chief ministers' original intent, he held the governing ministers in low regard.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wuzong's enthronement had not been the chief ministers' wish, he held little regard for the men then in power.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，李德裕自淮南入輔政。

translations.literal: That autumn, Li Deyu came from Huainan to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Li Deyu came from Huainan to join the government.

sentences.zh: 九月，出嗣復為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Sifu was sent out as military governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Li Sifu was sent out as military governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 明年，誅樞密薛季稜、劉弘逸。

translations.literal: The following year, the Palace Secretaries Xue Jiling and Liu Hongyi were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the palace secretaries Xue Jiling and Liu Hongyi were put to death.

sentences.zh: 中人言：「二人頃附嗣復、李玨，不利於陛下。

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs said, "These two men lately attached themselves to Sifu and Li Jue, to Your Majesty's detriment."
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs said, "These two lately sided with Li Sifu and Li Jue, to Your Majesty's harm."

sentences.zh: 」武宗性急，立命中使往湖南、桂管，殺嗣復與玨。

translations.literal: Wuzong was impatient by nature; he immediately ordered palace envoys to Hunan and the Guiguan circuit to kill Sifu and Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong was hot-tempered by nature and at once ordered palace envoys to Hunan and Guiguan to kill Li Sifu and Li Jue.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔鄲、崔珙等亟請開延英，因極言國朝故事，大臣非惡逆顯著，未有誅戮者，願陛下復思其宜。

translations.literal: Chief ministers Cui Tan and Cui Gong urgently requested an audience in Yanying Hall, where they spoke at length of dynastic precedent—that no minister who was not markedly guilty of treason had ever been put to death—and asked the emperor to reconsider what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers Cui Tan and Cui Gong urgently requested an audience in Yanying Hall and spoke at length of dynastic precedent: no minister who was not openly guilty of treason had ever been executed. They asked the emperor to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 帝良久改容曰：「朕纘嗣之際，宰相何嘗比數。

translations.literal: After a long silence the emperor's expression changed and he said, "At the time of my succession, were the chief ministers ever counted among my number?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause the emperor's face changed and he said, "When I succeeded to the throne, were the chief ministers ever on my side?"

sentences.zh: 李玨、季稜志在扶冊陳王，嗣復、弘逸志在樹立安王。

translations.literal: Li Jue and Jiling intended to install the Prince of Chen; Sifu and Hongyi intended to establish the Prince of An.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Xue Jiling meant to install the Prince of Chen; Li Sifu and Liu Hongyi meant to establish the Prince of An.

sentences.zh: 立陳王猶是文宗遺旨，嗣復欲立安王，全是希楊妃意旨。

translations.literal: Installing the Prince of Chen was still according to Wenzong's dying command; Sifu wanted to install the Prince of An entirely to gratify Consort Yang's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Installing the Prince of Chen was still in accord with Wenzong's dying command; Li Sifu wished to install the Prince of An solely to please Consort Yang.

sentences.zh: 嗣復嘗與妃書云：『姑姑何不敩則天臨朝？

translations.literal: Sifu once wrote to the consort, saying, 'Aunt, why not follow Empress Wu's example and hold court?'
translations.idiomatic: Li Sifu once wrote to the consort: 'Aunt, why not take Empress Wu as your model and hold court?'

sentences.zh: 』」珙等曰：「此事曖昧，真虛難辨。

translations.literal: Gong and the others said, "This matter is obscure; truth and falsehood are hard to distinguish."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gong and the others said, "This matter is unclear; truth and falsehood are hard to tell apart."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「楊妃曾臥疾，妃弟玄思，文宗令入內侍疾月餘，此時通導意旨。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Consort Yang once lay ill; her younger brother Xuan Si was ordered by Wenzong to enter the palace and attend her illness for over a month—at that time he conveyed their intentions."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Consort Yang once fell ill. Wenzong had her younger brother Xuan Si enter the palace to attend her for more than a month, and at that time he carried their messages back and forth."

sentences.zh: 朕細問內人，情狀皎然，我不欲宣出於外。

translations.literal: I questioned the palace women in detail; the circumstances are perfectly clear. I do not wish to make this known outside.
translations.idiomatic: I questioned the palace women closely; the facts are perfectly clear. I do not wish to make this public.

sentences.zh: 向使安王得志，我豈有今日？

translations.literal: Had the Prince of An prevailed, would I be here today?
translations.idiomatic: If the Prince of An had had his way, would I be emperor today?

sentences.zh: 然為卿等恕之。

translations.literal: Yet for your sake I shall pardon them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for your sake I will spare them.

sentences.zh: 」乃追潭、桂二中使，再貶嗣復潮州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recalled the envoys to Tan and Gui, and Sifu was demoted again to prefect of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then recalled the envoys bound for Tan and Gui, and Li Sifu was demoted again to prefect of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，徵拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Sifu was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, Li Sifu was summoned and appointed minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: ，自潮陽還，至岳州病，一日而卒，時年六十六。

translations.literal: Returning from Chaoyang, he fell ill at Yuezhou and died within a day, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back from Chaoyang he fell ill at Yuezhou and died within a day, at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈左僕射，謚曰孝穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Left Vice Director and the posthumous name Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Left Vice Director and given the posthumous name Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 子損、授、技、拭、捴，而授最賢。

translations.literal: His sons were Sun, Shou, Ji, Shi, and Zong, of whom Shou was the most worthy.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Sun, Shou, Ji, Shi, and Zong; of them Shou was the most worthy.

sentences.zh: 授，字得符，進士擢第，釋褐從事諸侯府，入為鄠縣尉、集賢校理。

translations.literal: Shou, styled Defu, passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving the burlap gown he served on staff in feudatory courts, then entered office as magistrate of Hu County and collator in the Office of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Shou, whose courtesy name was Defu, passed the jinshi examination. After taking his first office he served on the staffs of regional lords, then entered the capital as magistrate of Hu County and collator in the Office of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 歷監察御史、殿中，分務東臺。

translations.literal: He served as Imperial Censor and palace censor, with duties on the Eastern Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He served as imperial censor and palace censor, with duties on the Eastern Censorate.

sentences.zh: 再遷司勛員外郎、洛陽令、兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel, magistrate of Luoyang, and Assistant Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in turn to assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel, magistrate of Luoyang, and assistant director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 李福為東都留守，奏充判官，改兵部郎中，由吏部拜左諫議大夫、給事中，出為河南尹。

translations.literal: When Li Fu was Eastern Capital regent, Shou was recommended as his administrative aide; he was then made Director in the Ministry of War, and through the Ministry of Personnel was appointed Left Remonstrance Counselor and Attendant Censor, then sent out as Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fu served as regent of the Eastern Capital, Shou was recommended as his administrative aide. He was then made director in the Ministry of War, and through the Ministry of Personnel was appointed left remonstrance counselor and attendant censor before being sent out as intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 盧攜作相，召拜工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Lu Xie became chief minister, Shou was summoned as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xie became chief minister, Shou was summoned and appointed vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯京師，僖宗幸蜀，徵拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao attacked the capital, Emperor Xizong fled to Shu; Shou was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue.
