translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao attacked the capital and Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Shou was summoned and appointed vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 以母病，求散秩，改秘書監分司。

translations.literal: Because his mother was ill, he requested a nominal rank and was made concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was ill, he asked for a nominal post and was made concurrent director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, he was appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When the court returned to the capital, he was appointed vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 宰相有報怨者，改左散騎常侍、國子祭酒，又轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: A chief minister bearing a grudge had him transferred to Left Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Imperial Academy, and later to Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister who bore a grudge against him had him transferred to left regular attendant and grand master of the Imperial Academy, and later to mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 從昭宗在華下，改刑部尚書、太子少保。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Zhaozong to Huaxia, he was made Minister of Justice and Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Emperor Zhaozong to Huaxia, he was made minister of justice and junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左僕射。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the title of Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 子煚，字公隱，進士及第，再遷左拾遺。

translations.literal: His son Jiong, styled Gongyin, passed the jinshi examination and was twice promoted to Left Supplementer.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiong, whose courtesy name was Gongyin, passed the jinshi examination and was twice promoted to left supplementer.

sentences.zh: 昭宗初即位，喜遊宴，不恤時事，煚上疏極諫，帝面賜緋袍象笏。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong first ascended the throne, he delighted in feasting and neglected affairs of state; Jiong submitted a memorial strenuously remonstrating, and the emperor personally bestowed on him a crimson robe and ivory tablet.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong first came to the throne he delighted in feasting and neglected affairs of state. Jiong submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance, and the emperor personally bestowed on him a crimson robe and ivory tablet.

sentences.zh: 崔安潛出鎮青州，辟為支使。

translations.literal: When Cui Anqian went out to command Qingzhou, he recruited Jiong as staff envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Anqian went out to command Qingzhou, he recruited Jiong as his staff envoy.

sentences.zh: 不至鎮，改太常博士。

translations.literal: Before reaching his post, Jiong was transferred to Doctor of the Court of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his post, Jiong was transferred to doctor of the Court of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 歷主客、戶部二員外郎。

translations.literal: He served as Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites for Receptions and in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant director in the ministries of rites for receptions and of revenue.

sentences.zh: 關中亂，崔胤引硃全忠入京師，乃挈家避地湖南，官終諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the Guanzhong region fell into chaos, Cui Yin brought Zhu Quanzhong into the capital; Jiong then moved his family to Hunan as a refuge, and his highest office was Remonstrance Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guanzhong region fell into chaos and Cui Yin brought Zhu Quanzhong into the capital, Jiong moved his family to Hunan for safety. His highest office was remonstrance counselor.

sentences.zh: 損，字子默，以廕受官，為藍田尉。

translations.literal: Sun, styled Zimo, received office by yin privilege and served as magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, whose courtesy name was Zimo, received office by yin privilege and served as magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 三遷京兆府司錄參軍，入為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Recorder in the Jingzhao prefecture government, then entered office as palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became recorder in the Jingzhao prefecture government, then entered office as palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 家在新昌里，與宰相路巖第相接。

translations.literal: His family residence in Xinchang Ward adjoined the mansion of Chief Minister Lu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His family home in Xinchang Ward stood next to the mansion of Chief Minister Lu Yan.

sentences.zh: 巖以地狹，欲易損馬廄廣之，遣人致意。

translations.literal: Yan, finding the land too narrow, wished to exchange Sun's stable to enlarge it, and sent a messenger to convey his wish.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan, finding his grounds too cramped, wished to swap Sun's stable for more space and sent a messenger to propose the exchange.

sentences.zh: 時損伯叔昆仲在朝者十餘人，相與議曰：「家門損益恃時相，何可拒之？

translations.literal: At the time more than ten of Sun's uncles and brothers held court office; they discussed together, saying, "The family's rise or fall depends on the current chief minister—how can we refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time more than ten of Sun's uncles and brothers held office at court. They discussed the matter together and said, "The family's fortunes depend on the current chief minister—how can we refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」損曰：「非也。

translations.literal: Sun said, "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Sun said, "No."

sentences.zh: 凡尺寸地，非吾等所有。

translations.literal: Every scrap of land is not ours to own.
translations.idiomatic: Not one inch of ground is truly ours to dispose of.

sentences.zh: 先人舊業，安可以奉權臣？

translations.literal: Our forefathers' holdings—how could we surrender them to a powerful minister?
translations.idiomatic: These are our forefathers' holdings—how could we hand them over to a powerful minister?

sentences.zh: 窮達，命也。

translations.literal: Poverty and success are a matter of fate.
translations.idiomatic: Rise and fall are a matter of fate.

sentences.zh: 」巖不悅。

translations.literal: Yan was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會差制使鞫獄黔中，乃遣損使焉。

translations.literal: When an imperial commissioner was assigned to investigate cases in Qianzhong, Sun was dispatched on that mission.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial commissioner was sent to investigate cases in Qianzhong, Sun was dispatched on that mission.

sentences.zh: 逾年而還，改戶部員外郎、洛陽縣令。

translations.literal: After more than a year he returned and was made Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue and magistrate of Luoyang county.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he returned and was made assistant director in the Ministry of Revenue and magistrate of Luoyang county.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部員外，出為絳州刺史。

translations.literal: He entered office as Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel and was sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel and was sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 路巖罷相，徵拜給事中，遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: When Lu Yan was dismissed from the chancellorship, Sun was summoned as Attendant Censor and promoted to Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Yan was removed from the chancellorship, Sun was summoned as attendant censor and promoted to intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 盧攜作相，有宿憾，復拜給事中，出為陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: When Lu Xie became chief minister, bearing an old grievance, Sun was again made Attendant Censor and sent out as military governor of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xie became chief minister, still bearing an old grievance, Sun was again made attendant censor and sent out as military governor of Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 時軍亂，逐前使崔蕘。

translations.literal: At the time the army mutinied and drove out the former commissioner Cui Rao.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the army mutinied and drove out the former commissioner Cui Rao.

sentences.zh: 損至，盡誅其亂首。

translations.literal: When Sun arrived, he executed all the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun arrived, he executed all the ringleaders of the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 逾年，改青州刺史、御史大夫、淄青節度使。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was made prefect of Qingzhou, Censor-in-Chief, and military governor of Zi-Qing.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was made prefect of Qingzhou, censor-in-chief, and military governor of Zi-Qing.

sentences.zh: 又檢校刑部尚書、鄆州刺史、天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was also made acting Minister of Justice, prefect of Yanzhou, and military governor of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made acting minister of justice, prefect of Yanzhou, and military governor of the Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 未赴鄆，復留青州，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: Before proceeding to Yan, he was again kept at Qingzhou and died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could proceed to Yanzhou, he was kept at Qingzhou and died there in office.

sentences.zh: 技進士及第，位至中書舍人。

translations.literal: Ji passed the jinshi examination and rose to Drafter in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ji passed the jinshi examination and rose to drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 拭官終考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Shi's last office was Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel for Merits.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's last office was assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel for merits.

sentences.zh: 捴終兵部郎中。

translations.literal: Zong's last office was Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's last office was director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 拭、捴並進士擢第。

translations.literal: Shi and Zong both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Zong both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 楊虞卿楊虞卿，字師臯，虢州弘農人。

translations.literal: Yang Yuqing—Yang Yuqing, styled Shigao, was a native of Hongnong in Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuqing—Yang Yuqing, whose courtesy name was Shigao, was a native of Hongnong in Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖燕客。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Yanke.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Yanke.

sentences.zh: 父寧，貞元中為長安尉。

translations.literal: His father Ning served as magistrate of Chang'an during the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning served as magistrate of Chang'an during the Zhenyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 少有棲遁之志，以處士徵入朝。

translations.literal: From youth he had a mind for reclusion; summoned as a hermit scholar he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he wished to live in seclusion; summoned as a hermit scholar, he entered court.

sentences.zh: 有口辯，優遊公卿間。

translations.literal: He was gifted with eloquence and moved at ease among high ministers and nobles.
translations.idiomatic: He was eloquent and moved at ease among high ministers and nobles.

sentences.zh: 竇參尤重之，會參貶，仕進不達而卒。

translations.literal: Dou Can especially valued him; when Can was demoted, he never advanced in office and died.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can especially valued him, but when Can was demoted he never advanced in office and died.

sentences.zh: 虞卿，進士擢第，又應博學宏辭科。

translations.literal: Yuqing passed the jinshi examination and also entered the examination for erudite learning and grand rhetoric.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing passed the jinshi examination and also entered the examination for erudite learning and grand rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 元和末，累官至監察御史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhe era, through successive promotions he reached the office of Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Yuanhe reign he had risen through successive promotions to imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 穆宗初即位，不修政道，盤遊無節，虞卿上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong first ascended the throne, he did not cultivate the way of governance and wandered without restraint; Yuqing submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong first came to the throne he neglected governance and wandered without restraint. Yuqing submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞鳶烏遭害則仁鳥逝，誹謗不誅則良言進。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when birds of prey fall victim, birds of virtue depart; when slander is not punished, good counsel advances.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when birds of prey are harmed, virtuous birds depart; when slander goes unpunished, good counsel finds its way forward.

sentences.zh: 況詔旨勉諭，許陳愚誠，故臣不敢避誅，以獻狂瞽。

translations.literal: Moreover, an imperial edict encouraged and instructed, permitting the stating of humble sincerity; therefore your servant dare not flee punishment and offers these rash and blind words.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty's edict encouraged frank speech and permitted humble sincerity; therefore I dare not shrink from reproof and offer these rash and blind words.

sentences.zh: 竊聞堯、舜受命，以天下為憂，不聞以位為樂。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when Yao and Shun received Heaven's charge, they took the realm as their worry and did not take the throne as their joy.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Yao and Shun received Heaven's mandate, they worried for the realm and did not rejoice in the throne.

sentences.zh: 況北虜猶梗，西戎未賓，兩河之瘡磐未平，五嶺之妖氛未解。

translations.literal: Moreover, northern barbarians still obstruct, western tribes have not submitted, the wounds of the two He regions remain unhealed, and the demonic vapors of the five Ling ranges are not yet cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the northern tribes still resist, the western tribes have not submitted, the wounds of the two He regions are not yet healed, and unrest in the five Ling ranges is not yet settled.

sentences.zh: 生人之疾苦盡在，朝廷之制度莫修，邊儲屢空，國用猶屈。

translations.literal: The people's suffering is everywhere present; the court's institutions go unreformed; frontier stores are repeatedly emptied; state revenue is still strained.
translations.idiomatic: The people's suffering is everywhere; the court's institutions lie unreformed; frontier stores are repeatedly emptied; and state revenue is still strained.

sentences.zh: 固未可以高枕無虞也。

translations.literal: Surely one cannot rest one's head high and be free of care.
translations.idiomatic: Surely one cannot rest easy and be free of care.

sentences.zh: 陛下初臨萬宇，有憂天下之志。

translations.literal: Your Majesty at first faced the myriad realms with a mind to worry for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first faced the myriad realms, you had a mind to worry for the empire.

sentences.zh: 宜日延輔臣公卿百執事，凝旒而問，造膝以求，使四方內外，有所觀焉。

translations.literal: You ought daily to extend audience to assisting ministers, nobles, and the hundred officials—listening with lowered fringe and questioning closely—to let all within and without see and take notice.
translations.idiomatic: You ought each day to receive your assisting ministers, nobles, and the hundred officials—listening attentively and questioning closely—so that all within and without may see and take heed.

sentences.zh: 自聽政已來，六十日矣，八開延英，獨三數大臣仰龍顏，承聖問。

translations.literal: Since You began to hear cases of governance, sixty days have passed; Yanying has opened eight times, yet only a few chief ministers have looked up at the dragon countenance and received the holy inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Since you began to hold court, sixty days have passed. Yanying Hall has opened eight times, yet only a few chief ministers have looked upon your countenance and received your questions.

sentences.zh: 其餘侍從詔誥之臣，偕入而齊出，何足以聞政事哉！

translations.literal: The rest—the attendants and edict drafters—enter together and leave together; how could they hear affairs of government!
translations.idiomatic: The rest—the attendants and edict drafters—enter together and leave together. How can they truly hear affairs of government?

sentences.zh: 諫臣盈廷，忠言未聞於聖聽，臣實羞之。

translations.literal: Remonstrance counselors fill the court, yet loyal words have not reached Your Majesty's holy hearing—your servant is truly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance counselors fill the court, yet loyal words have not reached your ears—I am truly ashamed.

sentences.zh: 蓋由主恩尚疏，而眾正之路未啟也。

translations.literal: Surely this is because imperial favor is still distant and the path for the upright masses has not yet been opened.
translations.idiomatic: Surely this is because your favor is still withheld and the path for upright counsel has not yet been opened.

sentences.zh: 夫公卿大臣，宜朝夕接見論道，賜與從容，則君臣之情相接，而理道備聞矣。

translations.literal: High ministers and grand counselors ought to be received morning and evening to discuss the Way, granted leisure in conversation—then the sentiment between ruler and minister would connect and the principles of governance would be fully heard.
translations.idiomatic: High ministers and grand counselors ought to be received morning and evening to discuss the Way, granted unhurried conversation—then the bond between ruler and minister would be joined and the principles of governance fully heard.

sentences.zh: 今自宰相已下四五人，時得頃刻侍坐，天威不遠，鞠躬隕越，隨旨上下，無能往來。

translations.literal: Now from the chief ministers downward, only four or five men at times receive a moment to sit in attendance; imperial majesty is not far off—they bow and tremble, rising and falling as ordered, unable to exchange words freely.
translations.idiomatic: Now from the chief ministers downward, only four or five men at a time may sit in attendance for a brief moment. Your majesty is close at hand—they bow and tremble, rising and falling at your word, unable to speak freely with you.

sentences.zh: 此由君太尊、臣太卑故也。

translations.literal: This is because the ruler is too exalted and the minister too humble.
translations.idiomatic: This happens because Your Majesty stands too far above your ministers, and they too far below you.

sentences.zh: 自公卿已下，雖歷踐清地，曾未祗奉天睠，以承下問，郁塞正路，偷安幸門。

translations.literal: From high ministers downward, though they have repeatedly occupied pure posts, they have never reverently received Heaven's favor to meet inquiries from below; the upright path is blocked and choked, and they seek ease at the gate of favor.
translations.idiomatic: From chief ministers downward, though they have repeatedly held honorable offices, they have never truly received your favor or answered your questions; the path of upright counsel is blocked, and they rest content at the gate of private advantage.

sentences.zh: 況陛下神聖如五帝，臣下莫能望清光。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty is divine and sage like the Five Emperors; ministers below cannot gaze upon the pure radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty's sage virtue rivals that of the Five Emperors, and your officials cannot even meet your gaze.

sentences.zh: 所宜周遍顧問，惠其氣色，使支體相輔，君臣喻明。

translations.literal: What is fitting is comprehensive consultation and inquiry, bestowing facial expression upon them, enabling limbs to assist one another, and ruler and minister to understand each other clearly.
translations.idiomatic: You ought to inquire of them widely and grant them unhurried audience, so that the whole body of government works as one and ruler and ministers understand each other clearly.

sentences.zh: 陛下求理於公卿，公卿求理於臣輩，自然上下孜孜相問，使進忠若趨利，論政若訴冤。

translations.literal: Your Majesty seeks governance from high ministers; high ministers seek governance from our sort—naturally above and below will diligently inquire of one another, making the offering of loyalty like rushing toward profit and discussing government like lodging a grievance.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty seeks good counsel from your chief ministers, and they in turn seek it from their subordinates, then naturally all ranks will diligently question one another, offering loyalty as eagerly as one pursues profit and debating policy as urgently as one pleads for justice.

sentences.zh: 如此而不聞過失、不致升平者，未之有也。

translations.literal: If it is like this yet one does not hear of faults and does not reach ascendant peace, there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: If matters stood thus and the throne still did not learn of its errors and the realm did not reach peace, it would be without precedent.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王，居危思安之心不相殊，而居安慮危之心不相及，故不得皆為聖帝明王。

translations.literal: Since ancient times emperors and kings—the mind of dwelling in peril and thinking of peace is not different, but the mind of dwelling in peace and considering peril does not reach one another; therefore not all could become sage emperors and enlightened kings.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times, every ruler facing danger has wished for safety, but few who dwell in safety have thought ahead to danger; for this reason not all have become sage and enlightened sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 小臣疏賤，豈宜及此，獨不忍冒榮偷祿，以負聖朝。

translations.literal: Your humble servant is lowly and base—how should I reach to this? Yet I alone cannot bear to accept glory in vain and steal salary, thereby failing the holy court.
translations.idiomatic: I am humble and unworthy to speak of such things, yet I cannot bear to accept rank and salary in vain and fail this sacred dynasty.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty consider it.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider this.

sentences.zh: 帝深獎其言。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply impressed by his memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋令奉使西北邊，犒賞戍卒，遷侍御史，再轉禮部員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was ordered to serve as envoy to the northwest frontier to reward the garrison soldiers; he was moved to Supervising Censor, then transferred again to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites and Compiler of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was sent as envoy to the northwest frontier to reward the garrison troops. He was promoted to supervising censor, then transferred to assistant director in the Ministry of Rites and compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 八月，改吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, he was changed to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was reassigned as assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: ，南曹令史李幹等六人，偽出告身簽符，賣鑿空偽官，令赴任者六十五人，取受錢一萬六千七百三十貫。

translations.literal: Six clerks of the South Bureau, including Li Gan, forged outgoing commission documents and seals, selling hollowly created false offices; they enabled sixty-five appointees to take up their posts and received sixteen thousand seven hundred thirty strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Six clerks of the South Bureau, including Li Gan, forged commission documents and seals and sold fraudulent appointments on the open market. Sixty-five men took up these bogus posts, paying a total of 16,730 strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 虞卿按得偽狀，捕幹等移御史臺鞫劾。

translations.literal: Yuqing investigated and obtained the false cases, arrested Gan and the others, and transferred them to the Censorate for interrogation and impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing uncovered the fraud, arrested Gan and his accomplices, and had them transferred to the Censorate for trial.

sentences.zh: 幹稱六人共率錢二千貫，與虞卿廳典溫亮，求不發舉偽濫事跡。

translations.literal: Gan claimed the six jointly collected two thousand strings of cash and gave them to Yuqing's office manager Wen Liang, seeking that the false and abusive matters not be reported and prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Gan claimed the six had pooled two thousand strings of cash and given them to Wen Liang, the chief clerk in Yuqing's office, in exchange for suppressing the investigation.

sentences.zh: 乃詔給事中嚴休復、中書舍人高鉞、左丞韋景休充三司推案，而溫亮逃竄。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict appointed Supervising Secretary Yan Xiufu, Vice Director in the Secretariat Gao Yue, and Left Vice Director Wei Jingxiu to serve as the Three Offices Investigation Commission, while Wen Liang fled and went into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Yan Xiufu, Gao Yue, and Wei Jingxiu to conduct a special commission of investigation, while Wen Liang fled.

sentences.zh: 幹等既伏誅，虞卿以檢下無術，停見任。

translations.literal: After Gan and the others had been executed, Yuqing was suspended from his current post for lacking method in inspecting his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: After Gan and his accomplices were executed, Yuqing was suspended from office for failing to supervise his staff properly.

sentences.zh: 及李宗閔、牛僧孺輔政，起為左司郎中。

translations.literal: When Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru directed government, he was raised to Director in the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru came to power, he was recalled as director in the Left Bureau.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，拜諫議大夫，充弘文館學士，判院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, he was appointed Remonstrance and Policy Advisor, made Academic Administrator of the Hongwen Institute, and put in charge of its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year he was appointed remonstrance and policy advisor, made academician of the Hongwen Institute, and put in charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉給事中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 七年，宗閔罷相，李德裕知政事，出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when Zongmin was removed as chief minister and Deyu took charge of government affairs, Yuqing went out as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after Zongmin left office and Li Deyu assumed power, Yuqing was sent out as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 虞卿性柔佞，能阿附權幸以為奸利。

translations.literal: Yuqing by nature was soft and sycophantic, able to fawn upon the powerful and favored to seek wicked profit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing was by nature supple and sycophantic, skilled at currying favor with the powerful for illicit gain.

sentences.zh: 每歲銓曹貢部，為舉選人馳走取科第，占員闕，無不得其所欲；

translations.literal: Every year at the Board of Appointments and the Examination Department, he raced about for candidates in the selection process to obtain examination ranks and seize vacant posts, never failing to get what they desired;
translations.idiomatic: Each year during the selection and examination season he worked the appointments bureaucracy on behalf of candidates—securing ranks, claiming vacancies—always getting them what they wanted;

sentences.zh: 升沈取舍，出其脣吻。

translations.literal: Promotion, demotion, acceptance, and rejection issued from his lips.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions, demotions, and appointments alike depended on his word.

sentences.zh: 而李宗閔待之如骨肉，以能朋比唱和，故時號黨魁。

translations.literal: Moreover Li Zongmin treated him as kin, and because he could band together and sing in chorus, he was at the time called the faction chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin treated him as family, and because he excelled at building factional alliances, he was known at the time as the leader of the clique.

sentences.zh: 八年，宗閔復入相，尋召為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Zongmin returned to office as chief minister, and shortly Yuqing was summoned as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when Zongmin returned as chief minister, Yuqing was soon recalled as vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year, he was appointed Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year he was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，京師訛言鄭註為上合金丹，須小兒心肝，密旨捕小兒無算。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month, a rumor spread in the capital that Zheng Zhu, to compound an elixir for the emperor, required the heart and liver of small children; by secret edict children were seized without count.
translations.idiomatic: That June a rumor swept the capital that Zheng Zhu was compounding an elixir of immortality for the emperor and needed the hearts and livers of children; by secret order countless children were seized.

sentences.zh: 民間相告語，扃鎖小兒甚密，街肆洶洶。

translations.literal: Among the people word spread mutually; children were bolted and locked away very tightly, and the streets and markets were in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Panicked whispers passed from house to house, parents locked their children indoors, and the streets seethed with alarm.

sentences.zh: 上聞之不悅，鄭註頗不自安。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he was displeased, and Zheng Zhu was quite ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he was displeased, and Zheng Zhu grew deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李固言素嫉虞卿朋黨，乃奏曰：「臣昨窮問其由，此語出於京兆尹從人，因此扇於都下。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Guyan, who had long detested Yuqing's faction, memorialized, saying: "Your servant yesterday thoroughly inquired into its origin—this talk issued from the attendants of the Metropolitan Governor; thereby it was fanned throughout the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Guyan, who had long resented Yuqing's faction, memorialized: "Yesterday I pursued this to its source. The rumor originated with the metropolitan governor's attendants and was spread throughout the capital from there.

sentences.zh: 」上怒，即令收虞卿下獄。

translations.literal: " The emperor was angry and immediately ordered Yuqing seized and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was furious and ordered Yuqing arrested at once.

sentences.zh: 虞卿弟漢公並男知進等八人自系，撾鼓訴冤，詔虞卿歸私第。

translations.literal: Yuqing's younger brother Han Gong together with his sons Zhijin and seven others bound themselves and beat the appeal drum to plead injustice; an edict ordered Yuqing to return to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing's brother Han Gong and his sons, including Zhijin—eight men in all—bound themselves and beat the drum of appeal to protest his innocence. An edict then allowed Yuqing to return home.

sentences.zh: 翌日，貶虔州司馬，再貶虔州司戶，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: The next day he was demoted to army adjutant of Qianzhou, then demoted again to registrar of Qianzhou, and died in his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was demoted to army adjutant of Qianzhou, demoted again to registrar of the same prefecture, and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 子知進、知退、堪，弟漢公，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: His sons Zhijin, Zhihui, and Kan, and his younger brother Han Gong all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhijin, Zhihui, and Kan, together with his brother Han Gong, all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 知退歷都官、戶部二郎中；

translations.literal: Zhihui successively served as Director in the Ministry of Justice for Punishments and in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihui served successively as director in the Ministries of Justice and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 堪庫部、吏部二員外郎。

translations.literal: Kan served as Assistant Director in the Treasury Department and in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Kan served as assistant director in the Treasury Department and the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 虞卿弟 漢公漢公，擢進士第，又書判拔萃，釋褐為李絳興元從事。

translations.literal: Yuqing's younger brother Han Gong—Han Gong passed the jinshi examination, also excelled in the document-judgment examination, and upon leaving office dress served as staff officer to Li Jiang in Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing's younger brother Han Gong passed the jinshi examination, distinguished himself in the document-judgment examination, and took his first post as a staff officer to Li Jiang at Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 絳遇害，漢公遁而獲免。

translations.literal: When Jiang met calamity, Han Gong fled and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiang was murdered, Han Gong fled and survived.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部郎中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: In succession he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Compiler of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to director in the Ministry of Revenue and compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: ，遷司封郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel for Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel for enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 漢公子範、籌，皆登進士第，累辟使府。

translations.literal: Han Gong's sons Fan and Chou both passed the jinshi examination and were repeatedly invited to serve in frontier commission staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gong's sons Fan and Chou both passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly served on commission staffs.

sentences.zh: 虞卿從兄 汝士虞卿從兄汝士。

translations.literal: Yuqing's elder cousin Ru Shi—Yuqing's elder cousin Ru Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing's elder cousin Ru Shi.

sentences.zh: 汝士，字慕巢，進士擢第，又登博學宏詞科，累辟使府。

translations.literal: Ru Shi, styled Muchao, passed the jinshi examination, also passed the Examination for Erudite Learning and Magnificent Phrasing, and was repeatedly invited to serve in commission staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Shi, whose courtesy name was Muchao, passed the jinshi examination and the special erudite examination, and repeatedly served on commission staffs.

sentences.zh: 為右補闕。

translations.literal: He served as Right Supplements Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as right supplements censor.

sentences.zh: 坐弟殷士貢舉覆落，貶開江令。

translations.literal: Because his younger brother Yinshi failed re-examination in the tribute selection, he was demoted to magistrate of Kaijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Because his brother Yinshi was struck from the examination rolls upon re-examination, Ru Shi was demoted to magistrate of Kaijiang.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部員外，再遷職方郎中。

translations.literal: He entered court as Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue, then was transferred again to Director in the Ministry of War for Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as assistant director in the Ministry of Revenue, then was promoted to director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 七月，以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, retaining his original office he was put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was given charge of drafting edicts while retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 時李宗閔、牛僧孺輔政，待汝士厚。

translations.literal: At the time Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru directed government and treated Ru Shi generously.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru held power and treated Ru Shi with great favor.

sentences.zh: 尋正拜中書舍人，改工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was formally appointed Vice Director in the Secretariat and changed to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon formally appointed vice director in the Secretariat and promoted to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 八年，出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went out as prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was sent out as prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年九月，入為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, ninth month, he entered as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the ninth year he returned to court as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 七月，轉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was transferred to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，檢校禮部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: That year in the twelfth month he was made acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Zizhou, and military governor of Eastern Chuan in Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: That December he was made acting minister of rites, prefect of Zizhou, and military governor of Eastern Chuan in Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 時宗人嗣復鎮西川，兄弟對居節制，時人榮之。

translations.literal: At the time his clansman Sifu governed Western Chuan; the brothers faced each other holding military commands, and men of the time honored them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his clansman Sifu governed Western Chuan, so the two brothers held neighboring military commands—a distinction widely admired.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，入為吏部侍郎，位至尚書，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, ninth month, he entered as Vice Minister of Personnel, reached the rank of Minister, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year he returned as vice minister of personnel, rose to minister, and died.

sentences.zh: 子知溫、知遠、知權，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: His sons Zhiwen, Zhiyuan, and Zhiquan all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhiwen, Zhiyuan, and Zhiquan all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 汝士子 知溫知溫累官至禮部郎中、知制誥，入為翰林學士、戶部侍郎，轉左丞。

translations.literal: Ru Shi's son Zhiwen—Zhiwen rose through successive offices to Director in the Ministry of Rites and was put in charge of drafting edicts; he entered as Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue and was transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Shi's son Zhiwen rose through the ranks to director in the Ministry of Rites with charge of drafting edicts, then entered court as Hanlin academician and vice minister of revenue before becoming left vice director.

sentences.zh: 出為河南尹、陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Henan and commissioner of the Shan-Guo observation circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to serve as governor of Henan and commissioner of the Shan-Guo circuit.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校兵部尚書、襄州刺史、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: He was moved to acting Minister of War, prefect of Xiangzhou, and military governor of the Eastern Mountain-South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting minister of war, prefect of Xiangzhou, and military governor of the Eastern Mountain-South circuit.

sentences.zh: 知溫弟 知至知溫弟知至，累官至比部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: Zhiwen's younger brother Zhizhi—Zhiwen's younger brother Zhizhi rose through successive offices to Director in the Ministry of Revenue for Audits and was put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen's younger brother Zhizhi rose to director in the Ministry of Revenue for audits with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 坐故府劉瞻罷相，貶官。

translations.literal: Because former chief Liu Zhan was removed from office, he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When his former patron Liu Zhan was dismissed as chief minister, Zhizhi was demoted.

sentences.zh: 知至亦貶瓊州司馬。

translations.literal: Zhizhi was also demoted to army adjutant of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi was also demoted to army adjutant of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為諫議大夫，累遷京兆尹、工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered as Remonstrance and Policy Advisor and in succession was promoted to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as remonstrance and policy advisor and eventually rose to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 知溫、知至皆位至列曹尚書。

translations.literal: Zhiwen and Zhizhi both reached the rank of Ministers of the Six Boards.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zhiwen and Zhizhi rose to ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 汝士弟 魯士汝士弟魯士。

translations.literal: Ru Shi's younger brother Lushi—Ru Shi's younger brother Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Shi's younger brother Lushi.

sentences.zh: 魯士，字宗尹，本名殷士。

translations.literal: Lushi, styled Zongyin, original name Yinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Lushi, whose courtesy name was Zongyin, was originally named Yinshi.

sentences.zh: ，進士擢第，其年詔翰林覆試。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; that year an edict ordered re-examination by the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, but that same year the Hanlin Academy was ordered to re-examine the results.

sentences.zh: 殷士與鄭朗等覆落，因改名魯士。

translations.literal: Yinshi together with Zheng Lang and others failed re-examination; therefore he changed his name to Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: Yinshi, along with Zheng Lang and others, was struck from the rolls upon re-examination, after which he changed his name to Lushi.

sentences.zh: 復登制科，位不達而卒。

translations.literal: He again passed the special decree examination but died without attaining high office.
translations.idiomatic: He passed a special decree examination but died without reaching high office.

sentences.zh: 初汝士中第，有時名，遂歷清貫。

translations.literal: At first when Ru Shi passed the examination he had a reputation of the age and consequently passed through pure offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Ru Shi first passed the examination he enjoyed wide renown and rose through a succession of prestigious posts.

sentences.zh: 其年諸子皆至正卿，郁為昌族。

translations.literal: Within those years all his sons reached high ministerial rank, flourishing as a prosperous clan.
translations.idiomatic: Within a generation his sons had all risen to high ministerial rank, making theirs a flourishing family.

sentences.zh: 所居靜恭里，知溫兄弟，並列門戟。

translations.literal: The residence was at Jinggong Lane; the brothers Zhiwen and the others all displayed gate halberds in a row.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in Jinggong Lane, where Zhiwen and his brothers all displayed the gate halberds of high office side by side.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，昆仲子孫，在朝行方鎮者十餘人。

translations.literal: During the Xiantong era, among the brothers and their descendants, more than ten men served at court or in military prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong era more than ten members of the family held posts at court or as regional governors.

sentences.zh: 馬植馬植，扶風人。

translations.literal: Ma Zhi—Ma Zhi was a native of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhi—Ma Zhi was a native of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 父曛。

translations.literal: His father was Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Xun.

sentences.zh: 植，進士擢第，又登制策科，釋褐壽州團練副使。

translations.literal: Zhi passed the jinshi examination, also passed the Decree Examination for Policy Proposals, and upon leaving office dress served as deputy military training commissioner of Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi passed the jinshi and special policy examinations and took his first post as deputy military training commissioner of Shou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 得秘書省校書郎，三遷饒州刺史。

translations.literal: He obtained the post of collator in the Secretariat and was promoted thrice to prefect of Rao.
translations.idiomatic: He became a collator in the Secretariat and after three promotions was appointed prefect of Rao.

sentences.zh: 開成初，遷安南都護、御史中丞、安南招討使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he was moved to Protector-General of Annan, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and pacification commissioner of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng era he was appointed protector-general of Annan, vice censor-in-chief, and pacification commissioner of Annan.

sentences.zh: 植文雅之餘，長於吏術。

translations.literal: Beyond literary elegance, Zhi excelled at the craft of administration.
translations.idiomatic: In addition to his literary gifts he was accomplished in administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 三年，奏：「當管羈縻州首領，或居巢穴自固，或為南蠻所誘，不可招諭，事有可虞。

translations.literal: In the third year he memorialized: "Among the tribal chieftains under my jurisdiction in the tethered prefectures, some dwell in lairs to fortify themselves, and some are enticed by the southern barbarians—they cannot be summoned and instructed; the matter gives cause for concern.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he memorialized: "The tribal chieftains of the subject prefectures under my jurisdiction either hold themselves in mountain strongholds or are being incited by the southern tribes; they cannot be won over by persuasion, and the situation is worrisome.

sentences.zh: 臣自到鎮，約之以信誠，曉之以逆順。

translations.literal: Since your servant arrived at the command, I bound them by trust and sincerity and instructed them in rebellion and submission.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took up my post I have treated them with sincerity and made clear the consequences of loyalty and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今諸首領，總發忠言，願納賦稅。

translations.literal: Now all the chieftains have together uttered loyal words and wish to deliver taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Now all the chieftains have pledged their loyalty and offer to pay tribute and taxes.

sentences.zh: 其武陸縣請升為州，以首領為刺史。

translations.literal: Wulu County requests promotion to prefectural status, with the chieftain serving as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: They request that Wulu County be elevated to prefectural status and that the chieftain be appointed its prefect.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 又奏陸州界廢珠池復生珠。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that an abandoned pearl pool within the boundary of Luzhou had again produced pearls.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that an abandoned pearl bed within Luzhou's territory was once again yielding pearls.

sentences.zh: 以能政，就加檢校左散騎常侍，加中散大夫，轉黔中觀察使。

translations.literal: For able governance he was thereupon given the additional title of acting Left Regular Attendant of Loose Rein, promoted to Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and transferred to commissioner of the Qianzhong observation circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his capable administration he was given the additional title of acting left regular attendant, promoted to grand master of palace leisure, and transferred as commissioner of the Qianzhong circuit.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，入為大理卿。

translations.literal: During the Huichang era he entered as Chief Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang era he returned to court as chief minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 植以文學政事為時所知。

translations.literal: Zhi, for his literary learning and administrative affairs, was known to the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was renowned for his scholarship and administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 久在邊遠，及還朝，不獲顯官，必微有望，李德裕素不重之。

translations.literal: Long stationed on distant frontiers, when he returned to court he did not obtain a prominent office; he certainly looked faintly hopeful, and Deyu had never thought highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: After long service in remote regions, he returned to court without winning a prominent post; though he clearly hoped for one, Li Deyu had never held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，宰相白敏中與德裕有隙，凡德裕所薄者，必不次拔擢之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Chief Minister Bai Minzhong had a rift with Deyu; whoever Deyu had slighted was invariably promoted out of order.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, chief minister Bai Minzhong, who feuded with Deyu, promoted out of turn everyone Deyu had looked down upon.

sentences.zh: 乃加植金紫光祿大夫，行刑部侍郎，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhi was given the Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Girdle, acting as Vice Minister of Justice and serving as Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport in All Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was therefore made grand master of the gold seal and purple girdle, acting vice minister of justice, and commissioner for salt and iron transport.

sentences.zh: 轉戶部侍郎，領使如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, retaining the commission as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of revenue while continuing in his transport commission.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官同平章事，遷中書侍郎，兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly, retaining his original office, he was made Associate Counselor of State; he was moved to Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the chief council of state, was made vice director of the Secretariat, and concurrently minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 敏中罷相，植亦罷為太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: When Minzhong left office as chief minister, Zhi was also removed and made Mentor of the Heir Apparent, serving in the Eastern Capital office.
translations.idiomatic: When Minzhong left office, Zhi was also dismissed and given the nominal post of mentor to the heir apparent in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 數年，出為許州刺史、檢校刑部尚書、忠武軍節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: After several years he went out as prefect of Xu, acting Minister of Justice, and military governor and observation commissioner of the Zhongwu Army, among other duties.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was sent out as prefect of Xu, acting minister of justice, and military governor of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 大中末，遷汴州刺史、宣武軍節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dazhong era he was moved to prefect of Bian, military governor and observation commissioner of the Xuanwu Army, among other duties.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dazhong era he was transferred to prefect of Bian and military governor of the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮。

translations.literal: He died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 李讓夷李讓夷，字達心，隴西人。

translations.literal: Li Rangyi—Li Rangyi, styled Daxin, was a native of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rangyi—Li Rangyi, whose courtesy name was Daxin, was a native of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 祖悅，父應規。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Yue; his father was Yinggui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Yue; his father was Yinggui.

sentences.zh: 讓夷，擢進士第，釋褐諸侯府。

translations.literal: Rangyi passed the jinshi examination and, upon leaving probationary service, took his first appointment in a feudatory lord's staff office.
translations.idiomatic: Rangyi passed the jinshi examination and, upon leaving probationary service, took his first appointment on a regional lord's staff.

sentences.zh: 太和初入朝，為右拾遺，召充翰林學士，轉左補闕。

translations.literal: In the early Tahe era he entered court service, was made Right Remonstrance and Policy Advisor, was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician, and was transferred to Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tahe era he entered court service, was appointed remonstrance and policy advisor of the right, was summoned to serve as Hanlin academician, and was transferred to left supplementation censor.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷職方員外郎、左司郎中，充職。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments and Left Department Director, and held those posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to vice director in the Bureau of Appointments and left department director, continuing in both posts.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Remonstrance and Policy Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed remonstrance and policy advisor.

sentences.zh: ，以本官兼知起居舍人事。

translations.literal: With his existing rank he also took charge of the Diarist office.
translations.idiomatic: He also took charge of the diarist office while retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 時起居舍人李褒有痼疾，請罷官。

translations.literal: At the time Diarist Li Bao suffered a chronic illness and requested to resign his office.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the diarist Li Bao suffered from a chronic illness and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 宰臣李石奏闕官，上曰：「褚遂良為諫議大夫，嘗兼此官，卿可盡言今諫議大夫姓名。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Shi reported the vacant post. The emperor said: "When Chu Suiliang was remonstrance and policy grand master, he once also held this post. You may fully report the names of today's remonstrance and policy grand masters.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Shi reported the vacancy. The emperor said, "When Chu Suiliang served as remonstrance and policy advisor, he once also held this office. Report fully the names of the current remonstrance and policy advisors.

sentences.zh: 」石遂奏李讓夷、馮定、孫簡、蕭俶。

translations.literal: " Li Shi then reported Li Rangyi, Feng Ding, Sun Jian, and Xiao Shu.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Shi then nominated Li Rangyi, Feng Ding, Sun Jian, and Xiao Shu.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「讓夷可也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Rangyi will do.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Rangyi will do.

sentences.zh: 」李固言欲用崔球、張次宗。

translations.literal: " Li Guyen wished to use Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Guyen wanted to appoint Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「崔球遊宗閔之門，赤墀下秉筆記註，為千古法，不可用朋黨。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "Cui Qiu frequents Li Zongmin's faction. Standing below the red steps with brush in hand to record and annotate is a model for all ages—one must not employ partisan cliques.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "Cui Qiu moves in Li Zongmin's circle. Recording and annotating below the red steps of the throne hall is a precedent for all ages; one must not appoint men from partisan factions.

sentences.zh: 如裴中孺、李讓夷，臣不敢有纖芥異論。

translations.literal: Men such as Pei Zhongru and Li Rangyi—I dare not harbor even the slightest disagreement.
translations.idiomatic: As for men such as Pei Zhongru and Li Rangyi, I would not venture the slightest objection.

sentences.zh: 」其為人主大臣知重如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the esteem in which he was held by the sovereign and great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which rulers and chief ministers held him.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Drafting Secretary of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed drafting secretary of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以鄭覃此言，深為李玨、楊嗣復所惡，終文宗世，官不達。

translations.literal: Because of this remark by Zheng Tan, he was deeply hated by Li Jue and Yang Sifu, and throughout Emperor Wenzong's reign he never rose high in office.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Zheng Tan's remark, he was deeply resented by Li Jue and Yang Sifu, and throughout Emperor Wenzong's reign he never advanced far in office.

sentences.zh: 及德裕秉政，驟加拔擢，歷工、戶二侍郎，轉左丞。

translations.literal: When Li Deyu took power, he was suddenly promoted, successively serving as Vice Minister of Works and Vice Minister of Revenue, then transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deyu came to power, he was suddenly elevated, serving successively as vice minister of works and vice minister of revenue, then as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校尚書右僕射，俄拜中書侍郎，同平章事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and soon after was appointed Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and made co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to acting right vice director of the department of state affairs, and soon after was appointed vice director of the central secretariat and co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位罷相，以太子賓客分司卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded, he was removed as chief minister and died while serving as Prefectural Guest of the Crown Prince in a supervisory post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, he was removed from the chancellorship and died while serving as guest of the crown prince in a supervisory post at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 魏謩魏謩，字申之，鉅鹿人。

translations.literal: Wei Mo—Wei Mo, styled Shenzhi, was a native of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mo—Wei Mo, whose courtesy name was Shenzhi, was a native of Julu.

sentences.zh: 五代祖文貞公徵，貞觀朝名相。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Duke Wen Zhen, Wei Zheng, was a famous chief minister of the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor, Duke Wen Zhen Wei Zheng, had been a famous chief minister in the Zhenguan reign.

sentences.zh: 曾祖殷，汝陽令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yin was magistrate of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yin had been magistrate of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 祖明，亦為縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ming also served as a county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ming had also served as a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 父馮，獻陵臺令。

translations.literal: His father Feng was director of the Xianling Platform.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feng had been director of the Xianling platform.

sentences.zh: 謩，登進士第。

translations.literal: Mo passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Mo passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 楊汝士牧同州，辟為防禦判官，得秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: When Yang Rushi governed Tong Prefecture, he recruited Mo as defense staff judge and obtained for him the post of collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Rushi served as governor of Tong Prefecture, he recruited Mo as defense staff judge and secured for him the post of collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 汝士入朝，薦為右拾遺。

translations.literal: When Rushi entered the capital, he recommended Mo as Right Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Rushi came to court, he recommended Mo as remonstrance and policy advisor of the right.

sentences.zh: 文宗以謩魏徵之裔，頗奇待之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong, regarding Mo as a descendant of Wei Zheng, treated him with notable favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong, knowing Mo to be a descendant of Wei Zheng, treated him with special regard.

sentences.zh: 前邕管經略使董昌齡枉殺錄事參軍衡方厚，坐貶漵州司戶。

translations.literal: Formerly the Yong-Guan Circuit military governor Dong Changling had wrongly executed registrar Heng Fanghou and was demoted to registrar of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the military governor of the Yong-Guan circuit, Dong Changling, had unjustly executed registrar Heng Fanghou and was demoted to registrar of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 至是量移硤州刺史，謩上疏論之曰：「王者施渙汗之恩以赦有罪，唯故意殺人無赦。

translations.literal: At this time he was transferred laterally to governor of Xia Prefecture. Mo submitted a memorial arguing against it, saying: "The ruler grants broad clemency to forgive the guilty, yet deliberate homicide is never forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he was transferred to governor of Xia Prefecture. Mo submitted a memorial arguing against the appointment, saying, "A ruler grants sweeping clemency to forgive the guilty, but deliberate homicide is never forgiven.

sentences.zh: 昌齡比者錄以微效，授之方隅，不能祗慎寵光，恣其狂暴，無辜專殺，事跡顯彰。

translations.literal: Changling was recently recorded for minor merit and given a border post, yet failed to reverently honor the imperial grace, indulging his violence and wantonly killing the innocent—the facts are manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Changling was recently noted for minor merit and given a frontier post, yet failed to honor the imperial favor with due reverence, indulging his violence and killing the innocent at will—the facts are plain.

sentences.zh: 妻孥銜冤，萬里披訴。

translations.literal: His wife and children bore grievance and traveled ten thousand li to plead their case.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children nursed their grievance and traveled ten thousand li to plead their case.

sentences.zh: 及按鞫伏罪，貸以微生，中外議論，以為屈法。

translations.literal: When investigation proved his guilt, he was spared with a mere stay of execution, and both court and country regarded it as a bending of the law.
translations.idiomatic: When investigation proved his guilt, he was spared with only a light punishment, and both court and country regarded it as a bending of the law.

sentences.zh: 今若授之牧守，以理疲人，則殺人者拔擢，而冤苦者何伸？

translations.literal: If he is now given a governorship to rule over the weary people, then the killer is promoted—how can the wronged obtain redress?
translations.idiomatic: If he is now given a governorship to rule over a weary populace, then the killer is promoted—how can the wronged obtain redress?

sentences.zh: 交紊憲章，有乘至理。

translations.literal: This would entangle and disorder the statutes and violate fundamental principle.
translations.idiomatic: This would entangle and disorder the statutes and violate fundamental principle.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，乃改為洪州別駕。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, [the appointment] was changed to vice prefect of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the appointment was changed to vice prefect of Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞李孝本，皇族也，坐李訓誅，有女沒人掖廷。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Xiaoben, a member of the imperial clan, was implicated in Li Xun's execution, and his daughter was taken into the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Li Xiaoben, a member of the imperial clan, was implicated in Li Xun's execution, and his daughter was taken into the palace women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 謩諫曰：

translations.literal: Mo remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Mo remonstrated, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞治國家者，先資於德義；

translations.literal: "I have heard that those who govern a state must first rely upon virtue and righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard that those who govern a state must first rely upon virtue and righteousness;

sentences.zh: 德義不修，家邦必壞。

translations.literal: if virtue and righteousness are not cultivated, the family and realm will surely fall to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: if virtue and righteousness are not cultivated, the family and realm will surely fall to ruin.

sentences.zh: 故王者以德服人，以義使人。

translations.literal: Therefore the ruler makes men submit through virtue and moves them through righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the ruler makes men submit through virtue and moves them through righteousness.

sentences.zh: 服使之術，要在修身；

translations.literal: The art of submission and service lies in self-cultivation;
translations.idiomatic: The art of winning submission and service lies in self-cultivation;

sentences.zh: 修身之道，在於孜孜。

translations.literal: the way of self-cultivation lies in unceasing effort.
translations.idiomatic: the way of self-cultivation lies in unceasing effort.

sentences.zh: 夫一失百虧之戒，存乎久要之源。

translations.literal: The warning that one fault may undo a hundred accomplishments rests in the root of constancy over the long term.
translations.idiomatic: The warning that one fault may undo a hundred accomplishments rests in the root of constancy over the long term.

sentences.zh: 前志曰：「勿以小惡而為之，勿以小善而不為。

translations.literal: Former writings say: 'Do not do what is evil though it be small; do not fail to do what is good though it be small.
translations.idiomatic: Former writings say: 'Do not do what is evil though it be small; do not fail to do what is good though it be small.

sentences.zh: 」斯則懼於漸也！

translations.literal: ' This is to guard against the gradual slide!
translations.idiomatic: ' This is to guard against the gradual slide!

sentences.zh: 臣又聞，君如日焉，顯晦之微，人皆瞻仰；

translations.literal: I have also heard that the ruler is like the sun—whether bright or dim, the slightest change, all men observe;
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that the ruler is like the sun—whether bright or dim, the slightest change, all men observe;

sentences.zh: 照臨之大，何以掩藏？

translations.literal: the breadth of his illumination—how can it be concealed?
translations.idiomatic: the breadth of his illumination—how can it be concealed?

sentences.zh: 前代設敢諫之鼓，立誹謗之木，貴聞其過也。

translations.literal: Former dynasties set up drums for bold remonstrance and poles for posting criticism, valuing the hearing of their faults.
translations.idiomatic: Former dynasties set up drums for bold remonstrance and poles for posting criticism, valuing the hearing of their faults.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位以來，誕敷文德，不悅聲色，出後宮之怨婦，配在外之鰥夫。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's accession you have spread civil virtue abroad, taken no pleasure in music and women, released wronged women from the inner palace, and matched them in marriage to widowers outside.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession you have spread civil virtue abroad, taken no pleasure in music and women, released wronged women from the inner palace, and matched them in marriage to widowers outside.

sentences.zh: 洎今十年，未嘗采擇。

translations.literal: Down to the present, ten years on, you have never taken selections.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the present, ten years on, you have never taken selections from the palace.

sentences.zh: 自數月已來，天睠稍回，留神妓樂，教坊百人、二百人，選試未已；

translations.literal: Since several months ago Heaven's favor has shifted slightly—you have turned your attention to performers, and a hundred or two hundred from the Academy of Music have been selected and tested without cease;
translations.idiomatic: Since several months ago Heaven's favor has shifted slightly—you have turned your attention to performers, and a hundred or two hundred from the Academy of Music have been selected and tested without cease;

sentences.zh: 莊宅司收市，亹癖有聞。

translations.literal: the Palatial Estates Office has been buying up properties, and your special fondnesses have become known.
translations.idiomatic: the Palatial Estates Office has been buying up properties, and your special fondnesses have become known.

sentences.zh: 昨又宣取李孝本之女入內。

translations.literal: Yesterday the order went out to bring Li Xiaoben's daughter into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday the order went out to bring Li Xiaoben's daughter into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 宗姓不異，寵幸何名？

translations.literal: She shares the imperial surname—what name can be given to favoring her?
translations.idiomatic: She shares the imperial surname—what name can be given to favoring her?

sentences.zh: 此事深累慎修，有虧一簣。

translations.literal: This affair deeply undermines careful cultivation and falls short by a basketful of earth.
translations.idiomatic: This affair deeply undermines careful self-cultivation and falls short by a basketful of earth at the end of a mound.

sentences.zh: 陛下九重之內，不得聞知。

translations.literal: Within the innermost palace, Your Majesty did not hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Within the innermost palace, Your Majesty did not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 凡此之流，大生物議，實傷理道之本，未免塵穢之嫌。

translations.literal: Such conduct greatly provokes public criticism, truly injures the foundation of moral order, and cannot escape the taint of scandal.
translations.idiomatic: Such conduct greatly provokes public criticism, truly injures the foundation of moral order, and cannot escape the taint of scandal.

sentences.zh: 夫欲人不知，莫若勿為。

translations.literal: If one wishes that others not know, there is nothing better than not doing it.
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes that others not know, there is nothing better than not doing it.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：「止寒莫若重裘，止謗莫若自修。

translations.literal: As the proverb says: 'To stop cold, nothing is better than a heavy fur; to stop slander, nothing is better than self-reform.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says: 'To stop cold, nothing is better than a heavy fur; to stop slander, nothing is better than self-reform.

sentences.zh: 」伏希陛下照鑒不惑；

translations.literal: ' I humbly hope Your Majesty will examine this without confusion;
translations.idiomatic: ' I humbly hope Your Majesty will examine this without confusion;

sentences.zh: 崇千載之盛德，去一旦之玩好。

translations.literal: uphold your everlasting great virtue and set aside a moment's indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: uphold your everlasting great virtue and set aside a moment's indulgence.

sentences.zh: 教坊停息，宗女遣還，則大正人倫之風，深弘王者之體。

translations.literal: If the Academy of Music is halted and the clanswoman sent back, then the moral order will be greatly rectified and the dignity of kingship deeply affirmed.
translations.idiomatic: If the Academy of Music is halted and the clanswoman sent back, then the moral order will be greatly rectified and the dignity of kingship deeply affirmed.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝即日出孝本女，遷謩右補闕。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor released Li Xiaoben's daughter that same day and promoted Mo to Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor released Li Xiaoben's daughter that same day and promoted Mo to right supplementation censor.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔乃先祖貞觀中諫書十上，指事直言，無所避諱。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In former times your ancestor in the Zhenguan era submitted ten memorials of remonstrance, speaking directly to the matter at hand without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "In former times your ancestor in the Zhenguan era submitted ten memorials of remonstrance, speaking directly to the matter at hand without evasion.

sentences.zh: 每覽國史，未嘗不沈吟伸卷，嘉尚久之。

translations.literal: Each time I read the national histories, I have never failed to pause in contemplation and unfold the scroll, admiring him at length.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I read the national histories, I have never failed to pause in contemplation and unfold the scroll, admiring him at length.

sentences.zh: 爾為拾遺，其風不墜，屢獻章疏，必道其所以。

translations.literal: You serve as remonstrance and policy advisor; his spirit has not fallen. You have repeatedly submitted memorials, always stating your reasons.
translations.idiomatic: You serve as remonstrance and policy advisor; his spirit has not fallen. You have repeatedly submitted memorials, always stating your reasons.

sentences.zh: 至於備灑掃於諸王，非自廣其聲妓也；

translations.literal: As for training performers for the princes' households, this was not to enlarge your own troupe of musicians;
translations.idiomatic: As for training performers for the princes' households, this was not to enlarge your own troupe of musicians;

sentences.zh: 恤髫齔之宗女，固無嫌於徵取也。

translations.literal: in taking pity on a clanswoman still in childhood, there was naturally no impropriety in bringing her in.
translations.idiomatic: in taking pity on a clanswoman still in childhood, there was naturally no impropriety in bringing her in.

sentences.zh: 雖然，疑似之間，不可家至而戶曉。

translations.literal: Even so, in matters of suspicion and appearance, one cannot make every household understand.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, in matters of suspicion and appearance, one cannot make every household understand.

sentences.zh: 爾能詞旨深切，是博我之意多也。

translations.literal: You were able to make your words deeply felt—that shows how much you broadened my understanding.
translations.idiomatic: You were able to make your words deeply felt—that shows how much you broadened my understanding.

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 人能匪躬謇諤，似其先祖；

translations.literal: When a man can disregard himself and speak forthrightly, he resembles his ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: When a man can disregard himself and speak forthrightly, he resembles his ancestor;

sentences.zh: 吾豈不能虛懷延納，仰希貞觀之理歟？

translations.literal: can I not open my heart and welcome remonstrance, looking up to the governance of the Zhenguan era?
translations.idiomatic: can I not open my heart and welcome remonstrance, looking up to the governance of the Zhenguan era?

sentences.zh: 而謩居官日淺，未當敘進，吾豈限以常典，以待直臣！

translations.literal: Yet Mo's time in office has been brief and he is not yet due for promotion—shall I be bound by ordinary precedent when rewarding an upright minister!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Mo's time in office has been brief and he is not yet due for promotion—shall I be bound by ordinary precedent when rewarding an upright minister!

sentences.zh: 可右補闕。

translations.literal: He may be appointed Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He may be appointed right supplementation censor.

sentences.zh: 」帝謂宰臣曰：「昔太宗皇帝得魏徵，裨補闕失，弼成聖政。

translations.literal: " The emperor said to his chief ministers: "Formerly Emperor Taizong gained Wei Zheng, who remedied oversights and deficiencies and helped bring about sagely governance.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said to his chief ministers, "Formerly Emperor Taizong gained Wei Zheng, who remedied oversights and deficiencies and helped bring about sagely governance.

sentences.zh: 我得魏謩，於疑似之間，必能極諫。

translations.literal: I have gained Wei Mo—at the brink of doubtful appearances, he is sure to remonstrate to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: I have gained Wei Mo—at the brink of doubtful appearances, he is sure to remonstrate to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 不敢希貞觀之政，庶幾處無過之地矣。

translations.literal: I dare not hope for the governance of Zhenguan, yet perhaps I may stand where there is no fault.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not hope for the governance of Zhenguan, yet perhaps I may stand where there is no fault.

sentences.zh: 教坊副使雲朝霞善吹笛，新聲變律，深愜上旨。

translations.literal: Deputy Director of the Academy of Music Yun Zhaoxia was skilled at playing the flute, inventing new melodies and altering modes, deeply pleasing the emperor's taste.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy director of the Academy of Music Yun Zhaoxia was skilled at playing the flute, inventing new melodies and altering modes, deeply pleasing the emperor's taste.

sentences.zh: 自左驍衛將軍宣授兼揚府司馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted from Left Xiaowei Army General by direct imperial order to serve concurrently as Yang Prefecture military aide.
translations.idiomatic: By direct imperial order he was promoted from left Xiaowei army general to serve concurrently as military aide of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宰臣奏曰：「揚府司馬品高，郎官刺史叠處，不可授伶官。

translations.literal: The chief ministers reported: "The Yang Prefecture military aide is a high-ranking post occupied in turn by palace gentlemen and prefects—it must not be granted to a performer.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers reported, "The military aide of Yang Prefecture is a high-ranking post occupied in turn by palace gentlemen and prefects—it must not be granted to a performer.

sentences.zh: 」上意欲授之，因宰臣對，亟稱朝霞之善。

translations.literal: " The emperor wished to grant it, and in response to the chief ministers repeatedly praised Zhaoxia's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wished to grant it, and in response to the chief ministers repeatedly praised Zhaoxia's excellence.

sentences.zh: 謩聞之，累疏陳論，乃改授潤州司馬。

translations.literal: When Mo heard of this, he submitted memorial after memorial arguing against it, and [Zhaoxia] was instead appointed military aide of Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo heard of this, he submitted memorial after memorial arguing against it, and Zhaoxia was instead appointed military aide of Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 荊南監軍使呂令琮從人，擅入江陵縣，毀罵縣令韓忠，觀察使韋長申狀與樞密使訴之。

translations.literal: Retainer of Jingnan military commissioner Lü Lingcong entered Jiangling County without authorization, reviled and cursed the magistrate Han Zhong, and the observation commissioner Wei Chang submitted a report to the commissioner of military affairs to lodge a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: A retainer of Jingnan military commissioner Lü Lingcong entered Jiangling County without authorization, reviled and cursed the magistrate Han Zhong, and the observation commissioner Wei Chang submitted a report to the commissioner of military affairs to lodge a complaint.

sentences.zh: 謩上疏曰：「伏以州縣侵屈，只合上聞。

translations.literal: Mo submitted a memorial saying: "It is submitted that when prefectures and counties suffer encroachment and injustice, reports should ascend only to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Mo submitted a memorial saying, "It is submitted that when prefectures and counties suffer encroachment and injustice, reports should ascend only to the throne.

sentences.zh: 中外關連，須存舊制。

translations.literal: Links between the inner and outer courts must preserve the former institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Links between the inner and outer courts must preserve the former institutions.

sentences.zh: 韋長任膺廉使，體合精詳，公事都不奏聞，私情擅為逾越。

translations.literal: Wei Chang holds the post of integrity commissioner and ought in principle to be thorough and precise, yet he did not report the official matter and on private grounds overstepped by petitioning the military affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chang holds the post of integrity commissioner and ought in principle to be thorough and precise, yet he did not report the official matter and on private grounds overstepped by petitioning the military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 況事無巨細，不可將迎。

translations.literal: Moreover, whether matters are great or small, one must not curry favor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, whether matters are great or small, one must not curry favor.

sentences.zh: 縣令官業有乖，便宜理罪；

translations.literal: If a county magistrate's official conduct is at fault, he should be punished according to law;
translations.idiomatic: If a county magistrate's official conduct is at fault, he should be punished according to law;

sentences.zh: 監軍職司侵越，即合聞天。

translations.literal: if a military commissioner oversteps his duties, that should be reported to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: if a military commissioner oversteps his duties, that should be reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 或以慮煩聖聽，何不但申門下？

translations.literal: If one fears burdening the sacred ear, why not report only to the Secretariat?
translations.idiomatic: If one fears burdening the sacred ear, why not report only to the Secretariat?

sentences.zh: 今則首紊常典，理合糾繩。

translations.literal: As it stands, he has first disrupted regular precedent and should be called to account.
translations.idiomatic: As it stands, he has first disrupted regular precedent and should be called to account.

sentences.zh: 伏望聖慈，速加懲戒！

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Sacred Benevolence will swiftly impose punishment!
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Sacred Benevolence will swiftly impose punishment!

sentences.zh: 」疏奏不出，時論惜之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted it was not issued, and public opinion deplored it.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted it was not issued, and public opinion deplored it.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉起居舍人。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to diarist.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to diarist.

sentences.zh: 紫宸中謝，帝謂之曰：「以卿論事忠切，有文貞之風，故不循月限，授卿此官。

translations.literal: At his thanksgiving audience in the Purple Glazed Hall, the emperor said to him: "Because your remonstrance is loyal and earnest and carries the spirit of Duke Wen Zhen, I grant you this office without waiting for the monthly term limit.
translations.idiomatic: At his thanksgiving audience in the Purple Glazed Hall, the emperor said to him, "Because your remonstrance is loyal and earnest and carries the spirit of Duke Wen Zhen, I grant you this office without waiting for the monthly term limit.

sentences.zh: 」又謂之曰：「卿家有何舊書詔？

translations.literal: " He also said to him: "What old imperial writings and edicts does your family possess?
translations.idiomatic: " He also said to him, "What old imperial writings and edicts does your family possess?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「比多失墜，惟簪笏見存。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Many have been lost over time; only the court cap and ivory tablet remain.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Many have been lost over time; only the court cap and ivory tablet remain.

sentences.zh: 」上令進來。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered them brought in.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered them brought in.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「在人不在笏。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "It is in the person, not in the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "Honor rests with the man, not with the ivory tablet.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「鄭覃不會我意，此即《甘棠》之義，非在笏而已。
