translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Zheng Tan does not grasp my intent. This is the meaning of 'Sweet Pear Tree'—it is not merely a matter of the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Zheng Tan misses my point. This is the lesson of the Sweet Pear Tree—it is not about the tablet alone.

sentences.zh: 」謩將退，又召誡之曰：「事有不當，即須奏論。

translations.literal: " As Mo was about to withdraw, the emperor summoned him back and admonished him: "When something is not fitting, you must at once memorialize and discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: " As Mo was about to leave, the emperor called him back and warned him, "Whenever something is wrong, you must speak up in memorial at once.

sentences.zh: 」謩曰：「臣頃為諫官，合伸規諷。

translations.literal: " Mo said: "Your subject was recently a remonstrance official and ought to offer admonition and indirect criticism.
translations.idiomatic: " Mo said, "I was recently a remonstrance official, and it was my duty to offer frank counsel and pointed remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 今居史職，職在記言，臣不敢輒逾職分。

translations.literal: Now I hold a historiographer's post; my duty is to record speech, and your subject dares not casually overstep the bounds of office.
translations.idiomatic: Now I serve as a historiographer, and my duty is to record what is said. I dare not overstep my role on my own authority.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「凡兩省官並合論事，勿拘此言。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "All officials of the Two Departments alike should discuss affairs—do not be constrained by this remark.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Officials in both secretariats should all discuss state affairs. Do not hold yourself to that limit.

sentences.zh: 」尋以本官直弘文館。

translations.literal: " Shortly thereafter, with his existing office he served duty at the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon assigned to serve at the Hongwen Academy while retaining his existing post.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜諫議大夫，仍兼起居舍人，判弘文館事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Remonstrance Grand Master, still concurrently serving as diarist and adjudicating Hongwen Academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made remonstrance grand master, retained his post as diarist, and was put in charge of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 紫宸入閣，遣中使取謩起居註，欲視之。

translations.literal: Upon entering the Zichen Hall for the inner audience, the emperor sent a palace envoy to fetch Mo's daily record and wished to look at it.
translations.idiomatic: During an audience in the Purple Glazed Hall, the emperor sent a palace envoy to fetch Mo's court diary, intending to read it.

sentences.zh: 謩執奏曰：「自古置史官，書事以明鑒誡。

translations.literal: Mo held his ground and memorialized: "Since antiquity, historiographers have been established to record affairs so as to provide a clear mirror and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Mo stood firm and replied, "Historiographers have existed since antiquity precisely so that events may be recorded as a clear mirror and a warning.

sentences.zh: 陛下但為善事，勿畏臣不書。

translations.literal: Your Majesty need only do good deeds—do not fear that your subject will fail to write them down.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does only what is right, you need never worry that I will leave it unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 如陛下所行錯忤，臣縱不書，天下之人書之。

translations.literal: If what Your Majesty does is wrong and contrary, even if your subject does not write it, the people under Heaven will write it.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty acts wrongly, even if I fail to record it, the world will still write it down.

sentences.zh: 臣以陛下為文皇帝，陛下比臣如褚遂良。

translations.literal: Your subject takes Your Majesty to be Emperor Wen; may Your Majesty compare your subject to Chu Suiliang.
translations.idiomatic: I regard Your Majesty as another Emperor Wen; I ask only that you treat me as you would Chu Suiliang.

sentences.zh: 」帝又曰：「我嘗取觀之。

translations.literal: " The emperor again said: "I have once taken and looked at such records.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor added, "I have looked at such records before.

sentences.zh: 」謩曰：「由史官不守職分，臣豈敢陷陛下為非法？

translations.literal: " Mo said: "Because the historiographer failed to keep his duties, how could your subject dare to lead Your Majesty into an unlawful act?
translations.idiomatic: " Mo said, "Those historiographers failed in their duty. How could I allow Your Majesty to be drawn into what the law forbids?

sentences.zh: 陛下一覽之後，自此書事須有回避。

translations.literal: Once Your Majesty has read them, from that point onward the recording of affairs will necessarily involve avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: Once you have read the record, everything written thereafter will be shaped by what you are allowed to see.

sentences.zh: 如此，善惡不直，非史也。

translations.literal: If matters stand thus, good and evil will not be recorded straight—this is not historiography.
translations.idiomatic: If that happens, right and wrong will no longer be written plainly, and the record will cease to be history.

sentences.zh: 遺後代，何以取信？

translations.literal: Entrusted to later generations, by what means would they be persuaded to believe?
translations.idiomatic: How could future generations ever trust such a record?

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " With that, the emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 初立朝，為李固言、李玨、楊嗣復所引，數年之內，至諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When he first entered the court, he was brought forward by Li Guyen, Li Jue, and Yang Sifu; within several years he rose to Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took office, he was promoted by Li Guyen, Li Jue, and Yang Sifu, and within a few years reached the rank of remonstrance grand master.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，李德裕用事，謩坐楊、李之黨，出為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Li Deyu held sway; Mo was implicated as a partisan of Yang and Li and was sent out as prefect of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, Li Deyu dominated the government. Mo, counted among the Yang and Li faction, was posted out as prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊、李貶官，謩亦貶信州長史。

translations.literal: When Yang and Li were demoted in rank, Mo was also demoted to chief administrator of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang and Li were stripped of their offices, Mo was demoted as well, to chief administrator of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，白敏中當國，量移郢州刺史，尋換商州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Bai Minzhong directed the government; Mo was transferred within rank to prefect of Ying Prefecture and soon exchanged to Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to power and Bai Minzhong took control of the government, Mo was moved laterally to prefect of Yingzhou and soon transferred to Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，內徵為給事中，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was summoned from within to supervising secretary and was transferred to vice-director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled to court as supervising secretary and then promoted to vice-director of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 謝日，面賜金紫之服。

translations.literal: On the day he offered thanks, he was granted gold-and-purple robes in audience.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his audience of thanks, the emperor personally bestowed on him the gold-and-purple robes of high rank.

sentences.zh: 彈駙馬都尉杜中立贓罪，貴戚憚之。

translations.literal: He impeached the imperial son-in-law commandant Du Zhongli on charges of embezzlement, and the noble kin feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Du Zhongli, commandant-in-chief of horsemen and an imperial son-in-law, on charges of corruption, and even powerful clansmen were wary of him.

sentences.zh: 兼戶部侍郎，判本司事。

translations.literal: He was also appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and adjudicated affairs of that bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of revenue as well and placed in charge of that ministry's business.

sentences.zh: 謩奏曰：「御史臺紀綱之地，不宜與泉貨吏雜處，乞罷中司，專綜戶部公事。

translations.literal: Mo memorialized: "The Censorate is the seat of institutional discipline and is not suited to being mixed with treasury clerks. I request release from the vice-director's office so that I may exclusively administer Revenue business.
translations.idiomatic: Mo memorialized, "The censorate is the seat of institutional discipline. It should not be blended with the clerks who handle coin and grain. I ask to be relieved of the vice-directorship so I may devote myself wholly to revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官同平章事，判使如故。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, with his existing office he was made co-chancellor, and his commissioner duties remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made co-chancellor while retaining his existing post, and his other commissions remained the same.

sentences.zh: 謝日，奏曰：「臣無夔、契之才，驟叨夔、契之任，將何以仰報鴻私？

translations.literal: On the day he offered thanks, he memorialized: "Your subject lacks the talent of Kui and Xie, yet has suddenly received an appointment fit for Kui and Xie—by what means can I repay Your Majesty's vast grace?
translations.idiomatic: At his thanksgiving audience he memorialized, "I lack the wisdom of ministers such as Kui and Xie, yet I have suddenly been given a burden worthy of them. How can I ever repay Your Majesty's great kindness?

sentences.zh: 今邊戍粗安，海內寧息，臣愚所切者，陛下未立東宮，俾正人傳導，以存副貳之重。

translations.literal: The frontier garrisons are now roughly secure and peace prevails within the seas. What your foolish subject urgently cares about is that Your Majesty has not yet established the Eastern Palace, so that upright men may instruct the heir and preserve the weight of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The frontiers are calm and the realm is at peace. What weighs most on my mind is that Your Majesty has not yet named a crown prince and put upright mentors in the Eastern Palace to safeguard the institution of succession.

sentences.zh: 」因泣下。

translations.literal: " With that he burst into tears.
translations.idiomatic: " He broke down in tears as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 上感而聽之。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and accepted his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and took his advice.

sentences.zh: 先是，累朝人君不欲人言立儲貳，若非人主己欲，臣下不敢獻言。

translations.literal: Previously, successive sovereigns did not wish men to speak of establishing an heir apparent; unless the ruler himself desired it, ministers below dared not offer counsel.
translations.idiomatic: For generations, emperors had been unwilling to hear talk of naming an heir. Unless the ruler himself wished it, courtiers did not dare raise the subject.

sentences.zh: 宣宗春秋高，嫡嗣未辨，謩作相之日，率先啟奏，人士重之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was advanced in years and the legitimate successor had not yet been determined. On the day Mo became chancellor, he was the first to open the memorial on the matter, and men of stature respected him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was growing old, and the succession had not yet been settled. The day Wei Mo took office as chancellor, he was the first to raise the issue openly, and the court admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 尋兼集賢大學士。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was also appointed Grand Academician of the Jixian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became a grand academician of the Jixian Academy as well.

sentences.zh: 詹毗國獻象，謩以其性不安中土，請還其使，從之。

translations.literal: Zhanbi presented an elephant; Mo, because its nature was unsuited to the central realm, requested that the envoy be sent back, and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the kingdom of Zhanbi sent an elephant as tribute, Mo argued that the creature could not thrive in the central lands and asked that the envoys be sent home. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 太原節度使李業殺降虜，北邊大擾。

translations.literal: The military commissioner of Taiyuan, Li Ye, executed surrendered captives, and the northern frontier was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye, military commissioner of Taiyuan, executed prisoners who had surrendered, and the north erupted in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 業有所恃，人不敢非。

translations.literal: Li Ye had someone to rely upon, and men did not dare criticize him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye enjoyed powerful patronage, and no one dared speak against him.

sentences.zh: 謩即奏其事，乃移業滑州。

translations.literal: Mo at once memorialized on the matter, and Li Ye was transferred to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mo promptly memorialized on the affair, and Li Ye was reassigned to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 加中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大理卿馬曙從人王慶告曙家藏兵甲。

translations.literal: The grand judge of the Court of Judicial Review, Ma Shu, was denounced by his retainer Wang Qing, who reported that Shu's house concealed weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shu, chief judge of the court of judicial review, was accused by his retainer Wang Qing of hoarding arms and armor at home.

sentences.zh: 曙坐貶官，而慶無罪。

translations.literal: Shu was convicted and demoted in rank, yet Qing went unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was found guilty and demoted, while Qing went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 謩引法律論之，竟杖殺慶。

translations.literal: Mo cited the statutes in argument and in the end had Qing beaten to death with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Mo invoked the law in memorial and ultimately had Qing beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 進階銀青光祿大夫，兼禮部尚書、監修國史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Affairs and was concurrently Minister of Rites and supervisor of the compilation of state history.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master of glorious affairs with silver-blue insignia and made minister of rites while supervising the compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 修成《文宗實錄》四十卷，上之。

translations.literal: He completed the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong in forty scrolls and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He finished the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong in forty scrolls and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其修史官給事中盧耽、太常少卿蔣偕、司勛員外郎王諷、右補闕盧告、膳部員外郎牛叢，皆頒賜錦彩、銀器，序遷職秩。

translations.literal: The historiographers who had compiled it—Supervising Secretary Lu Dan, Vice Minister of Rites Jiang Xie, Outer Section Officer of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Feng, Right Supplementation Censor Lu Gao, and Outer Section Officer of the Ministry of Provision Niu Cong—were all granted brocade silks and silver vessels and were promoted in order of rank.
translations.idiomatic: The officials who had helped compile it—Lu Dan, Jiang Xie, Wang Feng, Lu Gao, and Niu Cong—were all rewarded with brocade silks and silver vessels and promoted in turn.

sentences.zh: 謩轉門下侍郎，兼戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Mo was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery and was concurrently Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was moved to vice director of the chancellery and made minister of revenue as well.

sentences.zh: ，以本官平章事、成都尹、劍南西川節度副大使知節度事。

translations.literal: He was also, with his existing office, made co-chancellor, prefect of Chengdu, and deputy military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit, managing circuit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed co-chancellor, prefect of Chengdu, and deputy commissioner of the Jiannan West circuit, with full authority over the circuit's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以疾求代，徵拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on account of illness he requested a replacement and was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he asked to be relieved on grounds of illness and was recalled as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 以疾未痊，乞授散秩，改檢校右僕射，守太子少保。

translations.literal: Because his illness had not yet healed, he requested an honorary nominal rank and was changed to honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State, serving as guardian of the Crown Prince's Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had not yet recovered, he asked for a purely honorary appointment and was made honorary right vice director of the department of state, serving as guardian crown prince junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 十二年十二月卒，時年六十六，贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twelfth year he died, aged sixty-six, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of the twelfth year at the age of sixty-six and was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 謩儀容魁偉，言論切直，與同列上前言事，他宰相必委曲規諷，唯謩讜言無所畏避。

translations.literal: Mo's bearing was imposing and his words cutting and direct. When he spoke on affairs before the emperor together with his colleagues, the other chief ministers invariably offered indirect remonstrance, but Mo alone spoke forthright remonstrance without fear or evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mo cut an imposing figure and spoke with blunt directness. When he and his fellow chancellors addressed the throne, the others usually couched their advice in roundabout terms, but Mo alone spoke with fearless, uncompromising candor.

sentences.zh: 宣宗每曰：「魏謩綽有祖風，名公子孫，我心重之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong often said: "Wei Mo abundantly carries his ancestor's spirit—he is a scion of a famous noble house, and I hold him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong often said, "Wei Mo truly inherits his family's legacy. As the son of a great house, he has my deep respect.

sentences.zh: 」然竟以語辭太剛，為令狐綯所忌，罷之。

translations.literal: " Yet in the end, because his language was too rigid, he was resented by Linghu Tao and was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end, however, his blunt speech earned the resentment of Linghu Tao, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 謩嘗鈔撮子書要言，以類相從，二十卷，號曰《魏氏手略》。

translations.literal: Mo once copied and extracted essential passages from various books, arranged them by category into twenty scrolls, and entitled the work Hand Compendium of the Wei Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mo once compiled essential passages from various books, grouped them by subject into twenty scrolls, and called the work Hand Compendium of the Wei Clan.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also left a collected writings in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子潛、滂。

translations.literal: His sons were Qian and Pang.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Qian and Pang.

sentences.zh: 潛登進士第。

translations.literal: Qian passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Qian passed the jinshi civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 潛子敖，韋琮甥。

translations.literal: Qian's son was Ao, a nephew of Wei Cong on his mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's son Ao was the nephew of Wei Cong.

sentences.zh: 後琮為相，潛歷顯官。

translations.literal: Later, when Cong became chancellor, Qian passed through distinguished offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong later rose to chancellor, Qian advanced through a series of high offices.

sentences.zh: 周墀周墀，字德升，汝南人。

translations.literal: Zhou Chi—Zhou Chi, styled Desheng, was a native of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chi—whose courtesy name was Desheng—was a native of Runan.

sentences.zh: 祖颋，父霈。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Feng and his father Pei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Zhou Feng and his father Zhou Pei.

sentences.zh: 墀，擢進士第，太和末，累遷至起居郎。

translations.literal: Chi passed the jinshi examination; by the end of the Taihe era he had been repeatedly promoted to Palace Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Chi passed the jinshi examination, and by the end of the Taihe reign he had risen through repeated promotions to palace diarist.

sentences.zh: 墀能為古文，有史才。

translations.literal: Chi could compose ancient-style prose and possessed historiographic talent.
translations.idiomatic: Chi wrote well in the ancient prose style and showed real talent as a historian.

sentences.zh: 文宗重之，補集賢學士，轉考功員外郎，仍兼起居舍人事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong valued him, appointed him an academician of the Jixian Academy, transferred him to outer-section officer in the Ministry of Personnel, and he still concurrently handled diarist duties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong valued him, made him an academician of the Jixian Academy, then promoted him to an outer-section officer in the ministry of personnel while keeping his duties as diarist.

sentences.zh: 冬，以本官知制誥，尋召充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In winter, with his existing office he was charged with drafting edicts, and shortly thereafter he was summoned to serve as a Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was assigned to draft imperial edicts while retaining his existing post, and was soon appointed a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷職方郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to director of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to director of the bureau of appointments.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，正拜中書舍人，內職如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year he was formally appointed Secretariat Drafter, and his inner-court duties remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year he was formally made secretariat drafter while retaining his inner-court posts.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，出為華州刺史、鎮國軍潼關防禦等使，改鄂州刺史、御史中丞、鄂嶽觀察使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, he was sent out as prefect of Hua Prefecture and military commissioner for the Zhenguo Army and Tong Pass defense, then was changed to prefect of E Prefecture, vice-director of the Censorate, and observation commissioner of E and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, he was posted out as prefect of Huazhou and commissioner for the Zhenguo army and Tong Pass defenses, then transferred to prefect of Ezhou, vice-director of the censorate, and observer of E and Yue.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遷洪州刺史、江南西道觀察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was transferred to prefect of Hong Prefecture and observation commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was moved to prefect of Hongzhou and observer of the Jiangnan West circuit.

sentences.zh: 大中初，檢校禮部尚書、滑州刺史、義成軍節度、鄭滑觀察等使、上柱國、汝南男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong era he was appointed honorary Minister of Rites, prefect of Hua Prefecture, military commissioner of the Yicheng Army, observation commissioner of Zheng and Hua, Upper Pillar of the State, and Baron of Runan with an enfeoffment of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong era he was made honorary minister of rites, prefect of Huazhou, military commissioner of the Yicheng army, and observer of Zheng and Hua circuits, with the titles upper pillar of the state and baron of Runan, enfeoffed with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 入朝為兵部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of War and adjudicated fiscal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as vice minister of war and put in charge of fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官同平章事，累遷銀青光祿大夫、中書侍郎、監修國史，兼刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, with his existing office he was made co-chancellor; he was repeatedly promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Affairs, Vice Director of the Secretariat, supervisor of the compilation of state history, and concurrently Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made co-chancellor while retaining his existing post, then rose through successive promotions to grand master of glorious affairs with silver-blue insignia, vice director of the secretariat, supervisor of the national history, and minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 罷相，檢校刑部尚書、梓州刺史、御史大夫、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: He was dismissed as chancellor, appointed honorary Minister of Punishments, prefect of Zi Prefecture, Grand Censor, and military commissioner of Jiannan East Sichuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving the chancellorship he was made honorary minister of punishments, prefect of Zizhou, grand censor, and military commissioner of the Jiannan East Sichuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 未行，追制改檢校右僕射，加食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Before he had set out, a follow-up edict changed his appointment to honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State and added five hundred households to his enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, a follow-up edict reassigned him as honorary right vice director of the department of state and raised his enfeoffment by five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 歷方鎮卒。

translations.literal: He passed through regional commands and died.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career in regional commands and died there.

sentences.zh: 崔龜從崔龜從，字玄告，清河人。

translations.literal: Cui Guicong—Cui Guicong, styled Xuangao, was a native of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guicong—whose courtesy name was Xuangao—was a native of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖璜，父誠，官微。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Huang and his father Cheng; their offices were lowly.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Cui Huang and his father Cui Cheng, both men of modest rank.

sentences.zh: 龜從，擢進士第，又登賢良方正制科，及書判拔萃二科，釋褐拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: Guicong passed the jinshi examination, also passed the decree examination for worthy and upright candidates, as well as the two examinations for document judgment and outstanding selection; upon leaving coarse cloth he was appointed Right Collector of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Guicong passed the jinshi examination, then the special decree examination for worthy and upright candidates, and also the document-judgment and outstanding-selection examinations. On entering official service he was appointed right collector of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: ，改太常博士。

translations.literal: He was then changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to erudite of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 龜從長於禮學，精歷代沿革，問無不通。

translations.literal: Guicong excelled in ritual learning and mastered the changes and developments of successive dynasties; there was no question he could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Guicong was a master of ritual studies and knew the evolution of institutions across dynasties in meticulous detail. There was almost nothing in the field he could not explain.

sentences.zh: 時饗宗廟於敬宗室，祝板稱皇帝孝弟。

translations.literal: At that time, when the ancestral temple was served at the chamber of Emperor Jingzong, the prayer tablet addressed the emperor as "filial brother."
translations.idiomatic: At the time, when sacrifices were offered in the ancestral temple at Emperor Jingzong's spirit tablet, the invocation addressed the emperor as "filial brother."

sentences.zh: 龜從議曰：「臣審祥孝字，載考禮文，義本主於子孫，理難施於兄弟。

translations.literal: Guicong argued: "Your subject has examined in detail the character xiang and the character xiao and searched through the ritual texts. Their meaning fundamentally applies to descendants, and it is logically difficult to apply them to brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Guicong argued, "I have examined the characters xiang and xiao against the ritual canon. Their meaning applies properly to descendants, not to brothers.

sentences.zh: 按《禮記》卜虞之文，子孫曰哀，兄弟曰某。

translations.literal: According to the text on divination for the Yu ceremony in the Book of Rites, descendants are called ai, and brothers are called by their personal name.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says that in the divination for the Yu rite, descendants are addressed as "ai" (the mournful), while brothers are addressed by personal name alone.

sentences.zh: 然則虞之稱哀，與祭之稱孝，其義一也。

translations.literal: Thus calling "ai" at the Yu and calling "xiao" at the sacrifice—their meaning is one.
translations.idiomatic: In the same way, the term "ai" used at the Yu rite and "xiao" used at the sacrifice ceremony express the same underlying principle.

sentences.zh: 於祖禰則理宜稱孝，於伯仲則止可稱名。

translations.literal: Toward ancestors and immediate forbears it is fitting to use xiao; toward elder and younger brothers one may only use personal names.
translations.idiomatic: Toward grandfathers and fathers it is proper to speak of filial devotion, but toward elder and younger brothers one may use only a personal name.

sentences.zh: 又東晉溫嶠議宗廟祝辭，於孝字非子者則不稱，傍親直言敢告。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the Eastern Jin Wen Jiao discussed ancestral temple prayer texts, holding that where the character xiao is concerned, if one is not a son one should not use it; for collateral kin one speaks directly and says "dare to report."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao of the Eastern Jin likewise argued that in ancestral temple invocations the word xiao should not be used except by a son, and that collateral relatives should address the spirit directly with "I dare report."

sentences.zh: 當時朝議，咸以為宜。

translations.literal: At the time the court's deliberations all considered this appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The court at the time unanimously agreed that this was correct.

sentences.zh: 今臣上考禮經，無兄弟稱孝之義；

translations.literal: Now, examining upward in the ritual classics, your subject finds no meaning in which brothers use xiao;
translations.idiomatic: When I turn to the ritual classics, I find no precedent for brothers to use the word xiao;

sentences.zh: 下徵晉史，有不稱傍親之文。

translations.literal: examining downward in Jin history, there are texts in which collateral kin are not so addressed.
translations.idiomatic: and when I consult Jin historical records, I find passages that likewise avoid addressing collateral relatives in that way.

sentences.zh: 臣謂饗敬宗廟，宜去孝弟兩字。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that in offering at the temple of Emperor Jingzong, the two characters xiao and ti should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore hold that in the sacrifice at Emperor Jingzong's temple, the words "filial brother" should be removed.

sentences.zh: 又以祀九宮壇，舊是大祠。

translations.literal: He also addressed the sacrifice at the Nine Palaces altar, which had formerly been classified as a great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He also weighed in on the sacrifice at the Nine Palaces altar, which had long been treated as a major state rite.

sentences.zh: 龜從議曰：「九宮貴神，經典不載。

translations.literal: Guicong argued: "The noble spirits of the Nine Palaces are not recorded in the canonical classics.
translations.idiomatic: Guicong argued, "The exalted spirits of the Nine Palaces are nowhere mentioned in the canonical classics.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，術士奏請，遂立祠壇。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, practitioners of the arts memorialized requesting it, and an altar for sacrifice was thereupon established.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign, occult specialists petitioned for its establishment, and a sacrificial altar was duly built.

sentences.zh: 事出一時，禮同郊祀。

translations.literal: The matter arose at a particular moment, yet its rites were treated the same as the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: It was a product of its moment, yet it was accorded the rites of a suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 臣詳其圖法，皆主星名，縱司水旱兵荒，品秩不過列宿。

translations.literal: Your subject has examined their charts and formulae: all are names of principal stars. Even if they govern flood, drought, warfare, and famine, their rank does not exceed that of ordinary constellations.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, the charts and formulae all name ordinary stars of the firmament. Even if they are said to govern flood, drought, war, and famine, their rank is no higher than the regular constellations.

sentences.zh: 今者，五星悉是從祀，日月猶在中祠，豈容九宮獨越常禮，備列王事，誡誓百官？

translations.literal: As matters stand, the Five Planets are all offered only as secondary sacrifices, and even the sun and moon remain classified as medium sacrifices—how can the Nine Palaces alone transgress regular rite, fully array the kingly ceremonies, and administer oaths of admonition to the hundred officials?
translations.idiomatic: Today even the Five Planets are offered only as secondary sacrifices, and the sun and moon remain at the level of medium rites. How can the Nine Palaces alone be allowed to overstep ordinary precedent, take on the full trappings of a royal ceremony, and impose sworn admonitions upon the entire bureaucracy?

sentences.zh: 尊卑乖儀，莫甚於此。

translations.literal: In high and low violating ritual propriety, nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing could violate the proper order of high and low more grossly than this.

sentences.zh: 若以嘗在祀典，不可廢除，臣請降為中祠。

translations.literal: If because it was once in the sacrificial canon and cannot be abolished, your subject requests reducing it to a medium sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: If it cannot be abolished because it was once entered in the sacrificial canon, I ask that it be reduced to a medium sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: " The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 龜從又以大臣薨謝，不於聞哀日輟朝，奏議曰：「伏以廢朝軫悼，義重君臣，所貴及哀，尤宜示信。

translations.literal: Guicong again, regarding the thanksgiving on a great minister's death and the failure to suspend court on the day mourning was heard, submitted a memorial stating: "Prostrate, your subject considers that suspending court to convey condolence bears the weight of the lord-minister bond; what is prized is reaching grief in time, and showing good faith is especially fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Guicong again addressed the court practice of acknowledging a great minister's death without suspending audience on the day the mourning news arrived. He submitted a memorial: "I humbly submit that suspending court to grieve carries the full weight of the bond between ruler and minister. The point is to respond while grief is fresh, and above all to act in good faith.

sentences.zh: 自頃已來，輟朝非奏報之時，備禮於數日外。

translations.literal: From recent times onward, suspension of court has not occurred at the time of the memorial report, and full rites have been observed several days later.
translations.idiomatic: In recent practice, court has not been suspended when the news was first reported, and the full mourning observances have been held days afterward.

sentences.zh: 雖遵常制，似不本情。

translations.literal: Although this follows regular regulation, it seems not rooted in genuine feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Though it follows established precedent, it hardly seems true to the heart of the matter.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢遠徵古書，請引國朝故事：貞觀中任瑰卒，有司對仗奏闕聞，太宗責其乖禮；

translations.literal: Your subject dares not cite distant ancient books and asks instead to invoke precedents of our dynasty: in the Zhenguan era when Ren Gui died, the appropriate offices reported the omission of news before the imperial presence, and Taizong reproached them for violating ritual;
translations.idiomatic: I will not reach back to remote antiquity, but cite our own dynasty's precedents: in the Zhenguan reign, when Ren Gui died, the responsible offices reported the lapse at imperial audience, and Emperor Taizong rebuked them for violating proper rite;

sentences.zh: 岑文本既歿，其夕為罷警嚴；

translations.literal: when Cen Wenben had already died, that very evening the palace guard was stood down;
translations.idiomatic: when Cen Wenben died, the palace guard was suspended that very evening;

sentences.zh: 張公謹之亡，哭之不避辰日。

translations.literal: when Zhang Gongjin perished, mourning for him did not avoid the Branch Day taboo.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhang Gongjin died, the court mourned him without observing the Branch Day restrictions.

sentences.zh: 是知閔悼之意，不宜過時。

translations.literal: From this one knows that the intent of compassion and mourning should not pass beyond the timely moment.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that sincere grief ought not to be delayed past its proper moment.

sentences.zh: 臣謂大臣薨，禮合輟朝。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that when a great minister dies, rite properly requires suspending court.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that when a great minister dies, ritual propriety requires suspending court.

sentences.zh: 縱有機務急速，便殿須召宰臣，不臨正朝，無爽事體。

translations.literal: Even if urgent state business arises and the side hall must summon the chief ministers without attending the formal audience, this does not impair the substance of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Even if urgent business required summoning the chief ministers to the side hall rather than holding formal audience, the substance of governance would remain intact.

sentences.zh: 如此，則由衷之信，載感於幽明；

translations.literal: If it is thus, then faith from the inner heart will be recorded and felt in the hidden and the manifest;
translations.idiomatic: Done this way, genuine sincerity would move both the living and the dead;

sentences.zh: 稱情之文，無虧於典禮。

translations.literal: and language matching feeling would not fall short of canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: and the language of the rites would honor both feeling and canonical precedent.

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「文武三品官薨卒輟朝。

translations.literal: " He further submitted: "When civil and military officials of the third rank die, court is suspended.
translations.idiomatic: " He also submitted: "When a civil or military official of the third rank dies, court is suspended.

sentences.zh: 有未經親重之官，今任又是散列者，為之變禮，誠恐非宜。

translations.literal: For those who have never been personally favored, whose present posts are also positions of loose standing—to alter ritual for them truly seems inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: To alter court ritual for officials who were never close to the throne, and who hold only perfunctory posts, would truly be inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 自今後，文武三品以上官，非曾任將相，及曾在密近，宜加恩禮者，餘請不在輟朝之限。

translations.literal: From now on, among civil and military officials of the third rank and above, except those who formerly served as generals or chancellors, or who were once in close attendance and deserve added favors of ritual, the rest should please fall outside the scope of court suspension.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, only third-rank civil and military officials who formerly served as generals or chancellors, or who had served in close attendance and merited special honors, should qualify for court suspension; all others should be excluded.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The emperor] approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 累轉考功郎中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Director in the Ministry of Personnel for Examinations and Compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to director in the ministry of personnel's examinations bureau and compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 九年，轉司勛郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel for Merit Records and charged with drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made director in the ministry of personnel's merit-records bureau and assigned to draft imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 十二月，正拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was formally appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: That December he received formal appointment as a secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 開成初，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era he was sent out as Prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng reign he was posted out as prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，人為戶部侍郎，判本司事。

translations.literal: In the third year, third month, he was recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue and adjudicated this ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year he was recalled to court as vice minister of revenue with charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 四年，權判吏部尚書銓事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was acting adjudicator of the Minister of Personnel's selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was given acting charge of the minister of personnel's selection examinations.

sentences.zh: ，為中書侍郎、同平章事，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Co-equal Chief Minister, and concurrently Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the secretariat, co-chancellor, and concurrently minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，撰成《續唐歷》三十卷，上之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year he completed compilation of Continuation of the Tang Calendar in thirty scrolls and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year he completed the thirty-scroll Continuation of the Tang Calendar and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 六年，罷相，檢校吏部尚書，汴州刺史、宣武軍節度觀察等使，累歷方鎮卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was dismissed as chancellor, appointed Honorary Minister of Personnel, Prefect of Bian Prefecture and Military Commissioner of the Xuanwu Army and observer of the circuit, passed through successive regional commands, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he left the chancellorship, became honorary minister of personnel, prefect of Bianzhou and military commissioner of the Xuanwu army, served through several regional postings, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 鄭肅鄭肅，滎陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Su—Zheng Su was a native of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Su was a native of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 祖烈，父閱，世儒家。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Lie and his father Yue; for generations the family were Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lie and his father Yue were scholars; the family had produced Confucian scholars for generations.

sentences.zh: 肅苦心力學。

translations.literal: Su toiled bitterly in mind and exerted himself in learning.
translations.idiomatic: Su applied himself to study with tireless discipline.

sentences.zh: ，擢進士第，又以書判拔萃，歷佐使府。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, also excelled in the document-judgment examination, and successively served as staff assistant in commissioners' offices.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, distinguished himself in the document-judgment examination, and served on the staffs of several commissioners.

sentences.zh: 太和初，入朝為尚書郎。

translations.literal: In the early Taihe era he entered court as a director in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe reign he entered court service as a director in the department of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉太常少卿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 肅能為古文，長於經學，左丘明、《三禮》、儀註疑議，博士以下必就肅決之。

translations.literal: Su could compose ancient-style prose and excelled in classical learning; on Zu Qiuming, the Three Rites, and disputed points in ritual commentaries, even erudites and those below had to take their questions to Su for resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Su wrote well in the ancient prose style and was deeply versed in the classics. On Zu Qiuming, the Three Rites, and disputed points in ritual commentaries, even court erudites routinely sought his judgment.

sentences.zh: 時魯王永有寵，文宗擇名儒為其府屬，用戶部侍郎庾敬休兼王傅，戶部郎中李踐方兼司馬，以肅本官兼長史，由是知名。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Lu Yong enjoyed favor; Wenzong chose eminent Confucians for his princely staff, appointing Vice Minister of Revenue Yu Jingxiu concurrently as the prince's tutor, Director in the Ministry of Revenue Li Jianfang concurrently as chief administrator, and Su with his existing office concurrently as chief secretary—and through this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Yong of Lu was in favor, and Emperor Wenzong selected leading scholars for his household. He appointed Yu Jingxiu, vice minister of revenue, as the prince's tutor; Li Jianfang, a director in the ministry of revenue, as chief administrator; and Su, retaining his existing post, as chief secretary. Su thereby won wider notice.

sentences.zh: 明年，魯王為太子，肅加給事中。

translations.literal: The following year when Prince Lu became crown prince, Su was additionally made Drafter in the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Prince Lu was made crown prince, Su was given the additional title of drafting counselor in the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 九年，改刑部侍郎，尋改尚書右丞，權判吏部西銓事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to Vice Minister of Punishments, then soon changed to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with acting charge of the western selection board of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to vice minister of punishments, then soon to right vice director of the department of state affairs, with acting charge of the western selection board.

sentences.zh: 開成初，出為陜虢都防禦觀察使、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he was sent out as Commissioner for the Defense and Observation of Shan and Guo Prefectures, concurrently Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng reign he was posted out as defense and observation commissioner of Shan and Guo, with the concurrent title of grand censor.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，召拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year he was recalled and appointed vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝以肅嘗侍太子，言論典正，復令兼太子賓客，為東宮授經。

translations.literal: Because the emperor considered that Su had once served the crown prince and his discourse was canonical and upright, he was again ordered concurrently to serve as Guest of the Crown Prince and to lecture in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Because Su had once served the crown prince and his teachings were sound and upright, the emperor again made him guest of the crown prince and assigned him to lecture in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 既而太子失寵，上不悅，有廢斥意。

translations.literal: Before long the crown prince lost favor; the emperor was displeased and had the intent to depose him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the crown prince fell from favor. The emperor was displeased and began contemplating his removal.

sentences.zh: 肅因召見，深陳邦國大本、君臣父子之義。

translations.literal: Su was thereupon summoned for audience and set forth deeply the great foundations of the state and the principles of lord-minister and father-son relations.
translations.idiomatic: Su was summoned to audience and spoke at length on the foundations of the realm and the obligations binding ruler and subject, father and son.

sentences.zh: 上改容嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor changed expression and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's manner changed and he expressed his approval.

sentences.zh: 而太子竟以楊妃故得罪。

translations.literal: Yet the crown prince in the end incurred blame on account of Consort Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end the crown prince was condemned because of Consort Yang.

sentences.zh: 乃以肅檢校禮部尚書，兼河中尹、河中節度、晉絳觀察等使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Su was appointed Honorary Minister of Rites, concurrently Prefect of the Capital of Hezhong, Military Commissioner of Hezhong, and observation commissioner of Jin and Jiang Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Su was then made honorary minister of rites, concurrently prefect of the Hezhong capital, military commissioner of Hezhong, and observer of Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，武宗思太子永之無罪，盡誅陷永之黨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang, Wuzong reflected on Crown Prince Yong's innocence and executed to the last those who had framed Yong's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huichang reign, Emperor Wuzong recalling Crown Prince Yong's innocence put to death all who had conspired against him.

sentences.zh: 朝議稱肅忠正，有大臣之節。

translations.literal: Court deliberation praised Su as loyal and upright, possessing a great minister's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held that Su had shown loyalty and integrity worthy of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 召拜太常卿，累遷戶部、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then repeatedly promoted to Minister of Revenue and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director of the court of imperial sacrifices and rose in succession to minister of revenue and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 五年，以本官同平章事，加中書、門下二侍郎，監修國史，兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, with his existing office he was made Co-equal Chief Minister, additionally given the two vice directorships of the Secretariat and the Chancellery, supervisor of the compilation of state history, and concurrently Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made co-chancellor while retaining his existing post, with additional appointments as vice director of both the secretariat and the chancellery, supervisor of the national history, and right vice director of the department of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 素與李德裕親厚。

translations.literal: From of old he had been close and intimate with Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been close to Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，德裕罷知政事，肅亦罷相，復為河中節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Deyu was dismissed from administering state affairs; Su also was dismissed as chancellor and again became military commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, Deyu was removed from power and Su was also dismissed from the chancellorship, returning to his post as military commissioner of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 以疾辭，拜太子太保，卒。

translations.literal: He declined on account of illness, was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned citing illness, was named grand preceptor of the crown prince, and died.

sentences.zh: 子 洎子洎，咸通中累官尚書郎，出為刺史。

translations.literal: His son Ji—Ji, during the Xiantong era through successive offices reached director in the Department of State Affairs, then was sent out as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji—during the Xiantong reign Ji rose through a series of posts to director in the department of state affairs, then served as a prefect.

sentences.zh: 洎子仁規、仁表，俱有俊才，文翰高逸。

translations.literal: Ji's sons Rengui and Renbiao both possessed outstanding talent; their literary compositions were lofty and unfettered.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's sons Rengui and Renbiao were both gifted writers whose prose was elegant and distinguished.

sentences.zh: 孫 仁規仁規累遷拾遣、補闕、尚書郎、湖州刺史、尚書郎知制誥，正拜中書舍人，卒。

translations.literal: Grandson Rengui—Rengui was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrance Officer, Supplementation Censor, Director in the Department of State Affairs, Prefect of Hu Prefecture, Director in the Department of State Affairs charged with drafting edicts, was formally appointed Secretariat Drafter, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Rengui rose through remonstrance officer, supplementation censor, and director in the department of state affairs to prefect of Huzhou, then returned as a drafting director before being formally appointed secretariat drafter; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 孫 仁表仁表擢第後，從杜審權、趙騭為華州、河中掌書記，入為起居郎。

translations.literal: Grandson Renbiao—after passing the examination Renbiao followed Du Shenquan and Zhao Zhi as chief secretary at Hua and Hezhong, then entered court as Palace Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Renbiao, after passing the examinations, served as chief secretary under Du Shenquan and Zhao Zhi in Huazhou and Hezhong, then entered court as palace diarist.

sentences.zh: 仁表文章尤稱俊拔，然恃才傲物，人士薄之。

translations.literal: Renbiao's essays were especially praised as brilliant and forceful, yet he relied on talent and was haughty toward others, and the gentry looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Renbiao's writing was admired as especially brilliant, but he flaunted his talent and treated others with contempt, and men of standing held him in low regard.

sentences.zh: 自謂門地、人物、文章具美，嘗曰：「天瑞有五色雲，人瑞有鄭仁表。

translations.literal: He claimed that his house's standing, his person, and his writings were all perfect, and once said: "Heaven's auspice has five-colored clouds; humanity's auspice has Zheng Renbiao.
translations.idiomatic: He considered his lineage, character, and literary gifts without equal, and once declared, "When heaven sends an omen it is a five-colored cloud; when earth sends one it is Zheng Renbiao.

sentences.zh: 」劉鄴少時，投文於洎，仁表兄弟嗤鄙之。

translations.literal: " When Liu Ye was young he submitted a piece of writing to Ji; the brothers Renbiao scoffed at and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: " In his youth Liu Ye submitted a literary work to Ji, and the Renbiao brothers sneered at it.

sentences.zh: 咸通末，鄴為宰相，仁表竟貶死南荒。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiantong Ye became chancellor, and Renbiao in the end was demoted and died in the southern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Xiantong reign Liu Ye became chancellor, and Renbiao was ultimately banished and died in the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 盧商盧商，字為臣，范陽人。

translations.literal: Lu Shang—Lu Shang, styled Weichen, was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shang—whose courtesy name was Weichen—came from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖昂，灃州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ang was Prefect of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ang had been prefect of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 父廣，河南縣尉。

translations.literal: His father Guang was magistrate of Henan County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang had served as magistrate of Henan county.

sentences.zh: 商，擢進士第，又書判拔萃登科。

translations.literal: Shang passed the jinshi examination and also passed the outstanding-selection examination in document judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Shang passed the jinshi examination and also distinguished himself in the document-judgment examination.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧力學，釋褐秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he exerted himself in learning; upon leaving coarse cloth he became Collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he studied with determination. On entering official service he was appointed collator in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 範傅式廉察宣歙，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Fan Fushi conducted incorrupt inspection of Xuan and She, he recruited Shang as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Fushi served as incorrupt investigator of Xuan and She, he recruited Shang as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 王播、段文昌相繼鎮西蜀，商皆佐職為記室，累改禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Wang Bo and Duan Wenchang successively governed western Shu; Shang in each case served as staff secretary, then was repeatedly changed to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Bo and then Duan Wenchang served in succession as governors of western Shu, Shang served on each man's staff as secretary. He later rose to assistant director in the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 入朝為工部員外郎、河南縣令，歷工部、度支、司封三郎中。

translations.literal: He entered court as Assistant Director in the Ministry of Works and magistrate of Henan County, and passed through the three directorships in Works, Fiscal Affairs, and Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as assistant director in the ministry of works and magistrate of Henan county, then served in succession as director in the ministries of works, revenue, and enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: ，改京兆少尹，權大理卿事。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Prefect of the Capital District and acting director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made vice prefect of the capital district and acting director of the court of judicial review.

sentences.zh: 開成初，出為蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he was sent out as Prefect of Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng reign he was posted out as prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 中謝日，賜金紫之服。

translations.literal: On the day of his middle audience of thanks he was granted golden-purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his formal audience of thanks he was granted robes of gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 初，郡人苦鹽法太煩，奸吏侵漁。

translations.literal: At first the people of the prefecture suffered because the salt laws were too burdensome and corrupt officials exploited them.
translations.idiomatic: At first the people of the prefecture suffered under onerous salt regulations and predatory corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 商至，籍見戶，量所要自售，無定額。

translations.literal: When Shang arrived he registered visible households, measured what each needed, and allowed self-sale without fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang arrived he registered households, assessed actual need, and allowed people to buy salt freely without fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 蘇人便之，歲課增倍。

translations.literal: The people of Su found this convenient, and annual revenue doubled.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Suzhou found this a relief, and annual tax revenue doubled.

sentences.zh: 宰相領鹽鐵，以其績上，遷潤州刺史、浙西團練觀察使。

translations.literal: The chancellor who headed the Salt and Iron Monopoly reported his achievement upward, and he was transferred to Prefect of Run Prefecture and Commissioner for Training and Observation of western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor in charge of the salt and iron monopoly reported his achievement, and Shang was promoted to prefect of Runzhou and training-and-observation commissioner of western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部侍郎，轉京兆尹。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of Punishments, then was transferred to Prefect of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice minister of punishments, then transferred to prefect of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 三年，朝廷用兵上黨，飛挽越太行者，環地六七鎮，以商為戶部侍郎，判度支，兼供軍使，軍用無闕。

translations.literal: In the third year the court deployed troops at Shangdang; rapid transport crossed the Taihang Mountains, encircling six or seven garrison commands. Shang was made Vice Minister of Revenue, adjudicated fiscal affairs, and concurrently served as army-supply commissioner; military supplies were not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the court waged war at Shangdang and urgent supply lines crossed the Taihang range through six or seven garrison zones, Shang was appointed vice minister of revenue with charge of fiscal affairs and concurrently army-supply commissioner, and military needs were fully met.

sentences.zh: 逆稹蕩平，加檢校禮部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: When the rebel Zhi was swept away and pacified, he was additionally appointed Honorary Minister of Rites, Prefect of Zi Prefecture, and Military Commissioner of Jiannan East Sichuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebel Liu Zhi was defeated and pacified, he was made honorary minister of rites, prefect of Zizhou, and military commissioner of Jiannan East Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，入為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, he entered court as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, he was recalled as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官同平章事、范陽郡開國公，食邑二千戶，加兼工部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, with his existing office he was made Co-equal Chief Minister, Duke of Fanyang Commandery with an enfeoffment of two thousand households, and additionally given concurrent service as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made co-chancellor while retaining his post, ennobled as duke of Fanyang commandery with two thousand households, and given the concurrent title of minister of works.

sentences.zh: 數年，檢校工部尚書，出為鄂嶽觀察使，就加檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: After several years he was appointed Honorary Minister of Works, sent out as Observation Commissioner of E and Yue, and on the spot additionally given Honorary Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was made honorary minister of works, posted out as observer of E and Yue circuits, and concurrently given the honorary title of minister of war.

sentences.zh: ，以疾求代，徵拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He sought replacement on account of illness and was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He requested relief on grounds of illness and was recalled as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，卒於漢陰驛，時年七十一。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year he died at Hanyin Post; he was seventy-one at the time.
translations.idiomatic: That eighth month he died at Hanyin post station, aged seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 子知遠、知微、知宗、僧朗、蕘。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhiyuan, Zhiwei, Zhizong, the monk Lang, and Rao.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Zhiyuan, Zhiwei, Zhizong, the monk Lang, and Rao.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：宗閔、嗣復，承宗室世家之地胄，有文學政事之美名，徊翔清華，出入隆顯。

translations.literal: The historian says: Zongmin and Sifu inherited the high lineage of an imperial-clan great house; they bore fine reputations in letters and governance, moved gracefully among the pure and splendid offices, and entered and left the court in lofty eminence.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Li Zongmin and Yang Sifu were heirs to an eminent imperial-clan house, famed for literary talent and administrative ability. They moved with ease through the highest offices and rose to the most exalted rank.

sentences.zh: 茍能義以為上，群而不黨，議太平於稷、契之列，致人主於勛、華之盛，遭時得位，誰曰不然？

translations.literal: If they could have taken righteousness as their guide, gathered without forming factions, deliberated on great peace in the company of Ji and Qi, and brought their sovereign to the splendor of Yao and Shun—encountering the age and obtaining position, who would say otherwise?
translations.idiomatic: Had they placed righteousness first, joined together without forming factions, debated the path to lasting peace alongside ministers like Ji and Qi, and guided their emperor toward the greatness of Yao and Shun—given their timing and rank, who would deny they might have done so?

sentences.zh: 而舍披鴻猷，狎茲鼠輩，養虞卿而射利，抗德裕以報仇。

translations.literal: Yet they abandoned spreading grand designs, dallied with these rat-like men, nourished a Lord Yuqing to shoot for profit, and opposed Deyu to repay old grudges.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they cast aside great statecraft, consorted with petty schemers, sheltered allies for profit like Zhao She nurturing Lord Yuqing, and battled Li Deyu to settle private scores.

sentences.zh: 矛盾相攻，幾傾王室，沒身蠻瘴，其利伊何？

translations.literal: Contradicting one another they attacked each other, nearly overturning the royal house; they ended their lives in malarial barbarian lands—what profit was there in this?
translations.idiomatic: Their factions clashed until the dynasty itself nearly toppled; they ended their lives in exile among malarial frontier wastes—what did they gain?

sentences.zh: 古者，廉、藺解仇，冀全國體，而邀歡釋憾，實亂大倫。

translations.literal: In antiquity Lian Po and Lin Xiangru dissolved enmity, hoping to preserve the integrity of the state; but seeking mutual delight and releasing resentment in fact disordered the great moral order.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Lian Po and Lin Xiangru set aside their feud to preserve the state—but trading favors to vent grievances in fact upended the bonds of propriety.

sentences.zh: 世道銷刓，一至於此！

translations.literal: The way of the world has been worn away—even to this point!
translations.idiomatic: Moral order had decayed until it came to this!

sentences.zh: 崔、魏二丞相，嘉言啟奏，無忝正人。

translations.literal: The two chief ministers Cui and Wei offered fine words in their memorials and did not disgrace upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Cui and Wei offered sound counsel in their memorials and lived as upright men without reproach.

sentences.zh: 墀、讓史才，肅之禮學，商之長者，或登三事，或踐六卿，以道始終，夫何不韙。

translations.literal: Chi and Rang possessed historiographic talent; Su had ritual learning; Shang had elder worthiness. Some reached the three high offices; some tread the six ministries. Beginning and ending in the Way—what was not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Chi and Rang had historiographic gifts, Su mastered ritual learning, and Shang was a man of steady virtue. Some reached the highest offices, others served across the six ministries, and each pursued the Way to the end—what fault could be found?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：漢誅鉤黨，魏破疽囊。

translations.literal: Encomium says: The Han executed the hooked faction; Wei broke the boil's pus-sac.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: The Han purged the faction cliques; Wei lanced the poisoned boil.

sentences.zh: 何鄧之後，二李三楊。

translations.literal: After He and Deng came the two Lis and three Yangs.
translations.idiomatic: After the He and Deng faction came the two Li and three Yang cliques.

sentences.zh: 偷權報怨，任國存亡。

translations.literal: Stealing power to repay grievances, they left the state's survival to chance.
translations.idiomatic: They seized power to settle scores, heedless of whether the realm survived or fell.

sentences.zh: 書茲覆轍，敢告巖廊！

translations.literal: Writing down this overturned cart-track, I dare inform the hall of cliff-side governance!
translations.idiomatic: I record this repeated folly as a warning to those who govern from the high halls of state.
